title: Big Fan!
body:
We’ve found JOON incredibly helpful for getting things done in our home! It’s engaging and motivating for our daughter, who’s very goal-oriented; she loves ticking off tasks and seeing her progress. The app’s colourful nature is visually appealing and fun, making the experience feel more like a game than a chore.

One feature we particularly love is the calendar for one-off tasks on specific dates (like “arrange a costume for the swimming carnival” or “pack extra clothes for the music excursion”) — it’s made staying organized so much easier- I put the reminder in as soon as I know a date so it’s off my to do list too. The “anytime” tasks are also fantastic for bigger jobs that don’t have a strict deadline or for things we want to save for a rainy day or school holidays when energy needs to be burned.

I also really appreciate the easy way to send encouragement — it keeps things positive and helps my daughter feel proud of her progress. As a mum, I feel less stressed, and it’s helped improve communication and independence. She’s more confident, too, getting that sense of accomplishment as she completes tasks.

Highly recommend JOON to any family looking to build positive habits and routines together!

title: Works on my kids aged 6 & 9
body:
I’ve waited a few months to review because I suspected the novelty would wear off and they would not care to work for coins any more. However, they still do care and are both now saving up their coins to purchase a beach permit worth 1000 coins! 

For those who are wondering if it would work on their kids, here are my thoughts:

- Foremost, my kids don’t usually otherwise get screen time (neither TV nor any screen-based games) so they are excited to get to play iPad for Joon. I think if they were used to  fancy video games then Joon would be too sedate for them, or if they were used to the dopamine hit of constant YouTube access, they would lose interest in Joon’s world quickly. Besides, I only let them play on Joon every few days anyway. That not only allows them to build up coins but also keeps the interest up. 

As it is, my kids have never played anything where there’s a world to freely explore, with characters to earn and buy accessories for, so they love that aspect. They also enjoy “seeing” each others’ doters wandering around their screen :-)

- I made all the quest completions under my control so they can’t just tap ‘done’ and get coins without my approval. You can make as many or as few quests as you wish, but I’ve made quests for every little thing I wish they would be more responsible for so it can be a lot for the parent to keep track of with reviewing them every day (tho you can scroll back to prior days). I don’t mind because I have been using a gamified task app for adults for myself for years, but my husband dislikes it, so it falls on me to keep track of all quests for both kids. It can be a lot. 

- The Joon creators are very responsive and constantly seek to improve, so I feel free to write to them with ideas. I had suggested a feature to turn on/off whether doters could be harmed or removed from the child’s custody if they don’t get fed or cared for after a while, because when my son realised they don’t die if he doesn’t feed them, he decided to never spend coins on food even though they are starving! He also doesn’t feel any urgency to do quests each day because of this.

title: 3 minutes and they were bored
body:
This company offers a 7 day trial, but you have to put in credit card details for the $140 a year subscription. 7 days for a single mum with 2 hyper boys is barely enough time to get it set up and see how it goes. I canceled the automatic subscription in 7 days and it cancelled my trial. 

They kept emailing offering an annual discount, I asked if there was a monthly fee I could try it for one month, they said no, then emailed a few days later saying yes, provided I took the offer within 24hrs. 

Go it all up, but as suspected my kids got bored with this in no time at all. I’m talking, within 5 and 10 minutes they moved straight to their other games. 

I suspect they are aware this can happened and why they push the larger annual fee instead of letting people pay monthly from the get go or offering a slightly longer trial.

title: Creating positive relationships
body: Writing down the tasks I ask my kids to do daily made me realise that I spend the majority of my interactions with them telling them what to do. Creating a profile on Joon has really changed that dynamic with my 12 ASD/ADHD child. She is able to see the daily expectations of her and self direct/control her schedule. After a fortnight of using Joon, she said to us last night, I’m going to do my homework, have a shower, feed the dog, walk the dog and put away my laundry now, so I have lots of time to enjoy playing later. I can guarantee this would not have happened prior to using Joon. Brad and his partners have been welcoming, generous and encouraging through this process and are genuine in their motives for this app. I highly recommend anyone with neurodiverse children who want to encourage them to be more independent and accountable, to try this.

title: Game Changer
body:
I was really apprehensive about this app at first. My first initial thoughts were that ‘gamifying’ my kids’ tasks would be encouraging my kids to seek rewards for every small aspect of their lives rather than teaching them perseverance. Or this app would just be one more app that was novel at first but would wear off quickly. I was very wrong.

First thing I must say, is that I signed up for this app out of desperation. Both of my kids have been diagnosed with ADHD and with them getting older they were starting to feel unmanageable. I was so tired of trying to motivate them and I desperately did not want to medicate them. I made them elaborate checklists and did everything I could to get them to follow a routine. They would do okay with things for a short time and then go back to being resistant and oppositional. I love them dearly and was getting tired of trying to negotiate everything or explain why things were important. So I thought I would try this app. 

I can say that this app is very well designed. It’s simple to use and doesn’t require a ton of effort once you’ve set up the initial tasks. You get lots of great options for creating tasks. How it limits the kids to do their tasks before they can use the game or purchase rewards is also truly genius. I was worried that it would make my kids super reward focused, but it doesn’t really. It’s simple in that they just earn coins and use those coins to spend in the game or purchase rewards like going to play with friends or having screen time. It’s just a more complex version of First-Then. 

And the results with my kids have been fantastic! I’m not even sure exactly what has made them change so quickly and dramatically. I think it’s just they they are able to see the results of what they are doing. I honestly don’t know, but they are calmer and more regulated than they have ever been. I was also worried that it wouldn’t stick and my kids would get bored of it and go back to their old ways, but they are still actually doing well with it after six weeks so far. They have even stopped fighting with each other so much. It’s mind blowing! 

This app has really worked for my kids. I wouldn’t call it a cure all, but it definitely has created a lot more harmony in our home and is steadily improving my kids’ regulation. I still have difficulties with certain things at times, but as I’ve gotten better at using the app’s features I have learned to tweak certain things that are getting us results. I really love that it’s not just an app for getting stuff done either. The categories for relationship building and focus & control have really made me more thoughtful about the tasks I give them and what I want to achieve with them. 

I am MORE than impressed with this app. It is absolute genius and I am so thankful for it! What I thought would just be another gimmick, turned out to be the best subscription I purchased this year! Thank you Joon!

title: You need to try this! 💕
body:

With the support of Brad I was able to get everything set up and working. My son ran to brush his teeth the first night as he saw he would get a reward. The next morning I had an early meeting and he did all his quests without anyone asking him to! I was blown away!!!! 
He loves to look after Mario and Moxie so far the characters he has created and likes to check in on them and tell others about them! 

Our mornings are vastly improved in the fact that I am not constantly asking him to put on clothes and get all his things together. 

What I think is really helping us is breaking it down into smaller quests- get dressed, daytime ears (cochlear implants), put on deodorant, eat your breakfast, put on socks! 
Adding your own quests and creating rewards makes it so customizable it has been great! 

When the coins add up the joy on his face is amazing! 

Our pediatrician even commented way to think outside the box! Thank you Joon team for coming up with this amazing tool! 🥰

They’re vacuuming, washing windows and doing their own dishes without me asking. My kids are aged 5 and 7, the 7 year old is more eager but the 5 year old wants to keep up to his big bro. Highly recommend this app
author: Anita MH

title: Great potential in this app
body: Motivating and interesting for my kiddo that doesn’t have any other video games but I think in time it will get a little boring if the game doesn’t add more features.  Right now the features that are accessible are feeding the pets and purchasing some costumes and plants for the land.  She has accumulated 5 pets rather quickly but hasn’t unlocked any other lands (it says she has to purchase a pass, but we don’t see a pass).  More challenging games and movement between different places would add excitement in the future.  The ability to add and customize quests is great and the parent portal is intuitive and easy to use.
author: LS801019

title: Life changer
body: This app has been a life saver for my family so much so that I talk about it and promote it to my co workers (we work in the field of youth and adults with diverse abilities. I am as well a Mandt System Trainer and have talked about this app as a preventative measure in behavior therapy due to the control it gives the kids over their lives, increasing independence and reducing stress on the parent or caregiver. It increases and teaches organizational skills, personal planning and introduces the concept of earning; using math skills, logic and strategies. This is the first app I have ever subscribed to but was hooked at the free trial how things were getting done, moods increased and it was fun. 100% thumbs up.

title: No Monthly Subscription

Seems like a money grabbing tactic since I am sure most users will have a similar experience and not end up using the app for longer than a few months. im sure because of this they will never release a monthly subscription since that wont make them enough revenue.

I would like for the app the be more smooth and quick. 

Also it’s very tiresome to confirm the quests have been done over and over. 

Three steps they are confirmed or collected and it’s waaayyyy too much for me. 

1. I wish he didn’t have to collect them again after I have confirmed them.

author: Skooc07

title: Needs improving
body:
This app is a good idea and has helped our 8yo AuDHD son with his routine. However I do have some issues. 
Some of the quest suggestions are pushing Neurotypical behaviours onto Neurodivergent children. For example have a conversation with eye contact without being reminded. This is surely not the point of the app. It just encourages masking in children that already struggle enough. There were many quests I simply scrolled past due to them being all about meeting the expectations of Neurotypical people. He does that all day at school. We do not expect this behaviour at home too. 
I also find the price too expensive. Ideally we would pay monthly. Incase our son stops finding the app useful. To pay monthly is extortionate compared to annually. I also think if you’re paying this much money for it, the app should be better. The children’s app is glitchy and looks cheaply made. 

We only paid as my son is enjoying it but I think there needs to be a lot of improvement.

author: Bbexy

title: Order is restored!
body:
We have two boys (10 and 6) who are both quite unpredictable and seemingly forgetful in the morning. They have to be told to get dressed, brush teeth, open curtain etc at least 5-10 times before they  might consider actually doing it. They have iPad but we limit the amount of gaming so it’s a treat, not the norm. Having a game like Joon is therefore quite exciting because they can play and check on it almost anytime in comparison to normal gaming time.
They really enjoy completing their tasks and discussing them. They still need to be reminded about some tasks on occasion but the difference is staggering. They both enjoy it and there’s a health sense of competition too without getting silly or nasty. From parenting user pov it’s great too. Very easy to set up, use, amend, add, remove etc. 
£70 is well worth the order that has been restored to the family to help start our day calmly and organised while we get ready for school and work together. I wish we had this a year ago!

title: Fantastic APP
body: We have a child with a PDA profile and JOON has been the best tool by far that is working for us as a family. Mornings are much calmer as we don't have to make requests as she reaches for the app first thing to tick off her tasks, look after her doters and importantly for her, gain points to redeem rewards. The app is easy to use and having the ability to create your own quests to meet the specific needs of your child works well. The app is helping her to manage her deep desire to spend quickly and save as this can be a challenge for her as she seeks a dopamine hit with a purchase and then crashes as she realises she doesn't have enough for the 'bigger' purchase. The key is setting small, medium and larger rewards as well as setting quests of different achieve levels. Make them too hard and it seems impossible, small quick wins give that desire to keep going. We negotiate quests and rewards and try to keep it fresh and relevant for what she is doing either now or in the not too distant future. There are of course the basic skills that we keep permanently. It's definitely a great tool to add to your kit when supporting your neurodiverse superstar! (and helps keep you a bit more sane)

title: ADHD Family Fun
body:
As a family of 6 with at least 4 of us with ADHD (both parents included), this app has been a lifesaver! 
I’m finding that we’re having to nag less and less, as the kids are developing their own autonomy through repeating regular daily patterns.
Also, for those who leave poor reviews because of supposed “negative impact of screen time/screen time addiction” etc - I’m an educator myself, and I’ve personally studied the impact of screen time. Suggesting that all screen time is bad, is like saying the internet is bad; it’s a tool and all about how you use it. Studies have proven games to significantly help neurodivergents, particularly those with ADHD and ASD, to navigate the day-to-day aspects of life that they find challenging (such as daily chores). Those of us with ADHD lack dopamine to help us complete simple tasks, and games can offer that through the reward aspect. Even just the opportunity to sequence tasks is a life saver, because those with ADHD struggle to organise thought processes and can become overwhelmed with everything that needs to be done. Having the opportunity to have a checklist for daily life means we can easily see the tasks ahead of us and feel the satisfaction of seeing those we have completed.
In fact, using this app has meant our kids are wasting LESS TIME in front of the TV and spending MORE TIME being productive and getting their homework and chores done. Not all screen time is “bad,” and we love that this app has brought order and productivity to our family - thank you!

title: Not a “family” ADHD app
body:
So this isn’t a family ADHD app as advertised. It is an app to make your ADHD child complete preferred tasks, tasks set by (probably) NT parents. 
I see how the novelty could motivate an ADHDer for a short time. The tasks set by these (probably) NT parents appear as *quests* for the ADHD child to overcome and accomplish. 
As an adult with ADHD, I see how the *quests* could trigger enough dopamine for an ADHD child (or me an ADHD adult) to complete. That dopamine triggered by novelty will probably drive that ADHD child to achieve the dictated *quests* for perhaps a few days. 
The *quests* will lose their novelty factor very quickly and stop triggering dopamine. 
Once the novelty and the dopamine reaction wears off, the *quests* will no longer be effective. 
The app tells you that this is THE solution for managing an ADHD brain, but that is untrue at best, and a bare faced lie at worst. 
I am middle aged and have struggled with ADHD that whole time. My child is teenaged and has struggled with ADHD that whole time. I believe these years of experience to be factual and insightful to those parents who don’t experience ADHD, and have an ADHD child. 
This app isn’t the solution it claims to be. 
The solution is to build momentum, not insist on motivation. ADHDers cannot experience motivation. The only way we can achieve multiple tasks is to build momentum. 
Make “momentum” your go-to word, and just pretend “motivation” does not exist. It isn’t a real word and it doesn’t mean a real thing. 
I, as an adult ADHDer, have to build momentum. I write my list for the day and always start with the easiest task. 
Sometimes that easiest task is just to fill the kettle and flick it to boil. The next easiest task would be to make a cup of tea. Next easiest could be to arrange the cups that need washing into one place. 
These simple tasks that build momentum may be tasks that NTs manage without even thinking. It should be easy to boil the kettle and make a simple cup of tea, right? You would probably make that cup of tea and balance your whole financial income and outgoings at the same time. 
No. It just isn’t that easy for us. We simply CANNOT function as expected. We can’t. We will destroy ourselves with thoughts of inadequacy because everyone else manages triple our maximum achievements. That’s inevitable, BUT if our parents accept that we are disabled and just boiling the kettle exhausts us, we grow from a place of acceptance, and that inevitable feeling of inadequacy is lessened. 
So, anyway, don’t use this app if your child is an ADHDer. They cannot possibly achieve with it for more than a few days. 
Instead, just accept that they are disabled and cannot achieve as much as you expect, of as fully as their same aged peers. 
Be a good parent to your disabled child. Do that by seeking knowledge and insight from adult ADHDers. We’re the only voices that count. 
Don’t immerse yourself in groups that consist of NT parents of ADHDers because the see our differences, but they cannot ever feel them. 
Good luck!

title: Pseudo-science.
body:
The unsuspecting parent’s nightmare: an app that promises to be ‘the only parenting app you’ll ever need’, is crammed full of jargon and ‘frameworks’ (which focus on conventional child development and pop psychology but conveniently nothing on gamification and tech engagement) and showcase a smiling team of ‘experts’ with plenty of letters after their names.

Despite citing esteemed academics such as ‘Chan & Zuckerberg’ 🤨 the reality is that there is precious little, if any, evidence from clinical trials that proves that gamification has any ability whatsoever to build long term character strengths or healthy children. There’s much more evidence of the damaging and addictive effects of tech, screens and notifications on child development, in particular contributing to attention and social skills deficits, plus nothing to suggest that gratification-based apps cultivate a long term propensity to develop skills and expertise.

Much as we’d love it to be so, you can’t gamify your children to healthy development. Put away the emperor’s new clothes, turn off notifications and trust that you don’t need Meta’s snake oil to be enough for your kids.

title: Joon for my 3 older kids, AsD and ADHD in the family
body:
Started to do joon a few weeks back. Since then I have seen a night and day improvement with my kids executive functioning. It used to be all I could do to get them to tidy their rooms after school or do their daily job, and forget making beds or even brushing teeth. Nag nag nag. Now however, my kids are motivating themselves to get stuff done to get coins. One has like 8 pets so far, another 5. The more they do the game, I need to put a few extra things on for them to earn more. 

But it doesn’t have to be jobs to put on, either. It can be mental health stuff, or exercise, etc, to get a few more coins in a fun way. I have one for the kids to finish their school drink bottle, bc they were getting migraines. 

They can play games, it’s sort of like neopets from the early 2000’s. You can set rewards for them to purchase with their coins as well. And if you really want to, I’m sure you could put yourself as a child too! 

We have AsD, adhd, Irlens x2, probable dyslexia, dyspraxia, and other stuff in our family to contend with. Believe me this isn’t a neurotypical family! And it works!

But once I’d set custom rewards that include fun family activities that she did want she has become really engaged in checking for quests, doing them and claiming rewards. The younger one is enjoying the game aspect of the app and I can’t believe that she’s actually saying things like “oh, I’ve gotto unload the dishwasher now because I want the coins”!! I’ve got ADHD too and the app is helping my planning and management and making day to day life easier because I don’t have to argue or even ask anymore. I guess it take the onus off and onto them. I’ve never been able to maintain star charts or my routines beyond the ones necessary to meet external obligations, like school. So so far Joon is flipping awesome. title: Well designed, Well research and it Works!
body:
I am not a huge fan of using games or points to reward behaviour and would always use incentive (ice cream etc) as sparingly as possible so a not encourage a transactional approach towards good behaviour. 

But when my daughter was diagnosed as borderline ADHD, I knew it was more than about standing on principle, but how to help her build stamina and good neurological connections to stay focus and attentive to the tasks at hand.

Joon has done this exceedingly well from the get go - was impressed by the onboarding process for the child - we had fun selecting our doter and it was exactly the right voice and companion that matched our daughter’s preferences. Then anchoring first with breathing exercises as a simple quest, then jumping jacks, before launching into my first simple quest - Speaking Graciousness without prompting.

Then suddenly the world of doter opens up with different ways to care for a virtual friend and going on quests together. And the script is also engaging and uplifting. 

There’s a lot more things that are deeply thought through - including the real world integration and joint quests with parents. My wife has now put in her own personal quests to eat mindfully and we suddenly opened up a new space to explore and discuss real world issues through the quests. Looking forward to the rest of the adventures together

title: Helpful, Kid-Friendly Task Manager
body:
We recently started using the Joon app after my wife returned to work, and it’s been a fantastic tool for helping our kids manage their tasks and homework independently. We were looking for a way to encourage more self-management without constant reminders, and Joon has really delivered.

Even though our kids don’t have ADHD, the app’s kid-friendly design, built-in rewards, and gamified approach have worked really well for motivating them. They actually enjoy checking off their to-do list and taking responsibility for their routines. It’s been great to see them develop a sense of ownership over their tasks. Highly recommend for any family looking to build independence and good habits in a fun, engaging way!

body:

Pros: overall easy chore management, kids and parents can all participate, rewards are nice and adjustable for lots of different purposes (trip to the candy aisle is a popular one here)

title: Great theory, kids abandoned after 1 month
body:
The idea behind this app is wonderful and has great potential. Unfortunately, it didn’t stick for my family. A monthly subscription option would have been appreciated or perhaps a 2-week trial to fully understand the app before committing to the full year cost $$$.

My suggestion would be to have the reminders/notifications to check tasks be within the children’s side of the app. I found that after the newness had worn off for the kids that I was back in nag mode to make them check the app. There is so much management needed on the parents’ side that it became too much of a task to maintain daily. It appears there is a great amount of customization that can be done, plus useful templates but I simply don’t have that much time to invest in learning. There’s gold in these hills if the app could lean in more on training the children how to make these habits and be accountable for checking off tasks themselves — and not just collecting rewards from the parents’ complex effort to build and maintain the checkboxes.

I appreciate the effort to help ADHD parents — keep refining it and you’ll be successful.

author: Prgreetings

title: Pros and Cons
body:
This app has been useful for keeping a steady time-based checklist for our neuro-divergent family. However, most days it becomes another task to make sure our child actually references and checks off the daily quests… but I don’t think that aspect would change with a different checklist system.

Some features have been useful: I like that there are two ways to access the app so we can keep our child’s app on one device and the parent portal on our own device. The doter chat feature has actually been really fun for our kiddo and I like that we can see it on the parent side. Caring for the doters has kept our child’s interest, especially since new ones hatch all the time. The custom reward system has been working well for us. Neat that we can add quests & rewards for parents too. 

For how much this app costs, there are aspects I wish were more user friendly: 
1. The custom quest “save template” doesn’t actually save, it doesn’t show up on the new quest screen. There are instructions how to find it and mine are simply not there. Which can be very annoying because it’s not super clear about how to make it repeat every day, and when you edit a quest you don’t have the option to retroactively repeat every day or duplicate.
2. The quest skill categories are nice but I wish we could sort the checklist by categories rather than only by time of day.
3. The games are not super educational and I wish they weren’t in the app at all.
4. I wish there was a more advanced reward option where users can make “payments” of coins to build up to a larger goal. Right now we have to make individual rewards that are “_x_ toward _goal_” and it’s not easy to count how many times it was purchased. The parent side shows individual line items for “purchased” and “used” so at first glance it looks like two separate purchases.
5. Different sort options in general would be better for quest checklist, and add a filter option.
6. It would be nice to make a quest that just has to be completed once a week, but not on a specific day. 
7. Some of the suggested most-used quests make me sad, because apparently lots of users don’t know how to make quests measurable/attainable/realistic for kids.

title: Sneaky subscription requirement
body:
1. Heads up: unless you are going to assign 7 or fewer tasks per day, don't bother downloading this. The app strings you along and lets you believe you'll be able to use its basics for free. It DOES pester you nonstop to upgrade/subscribe, but you can opt out initially. You get this all set up, the kid's game app installed, and your kid invested in using it, and THEN after the 7th completed task, it hits you with the subscription requirement to keep using it. Very aggravated at the old bait and switch tactics and will be uninstalling. 
2. Additionally: For an app that is supposed to help keep a kid on track, why on earth are there a myriad of extra coin-earning tasks built in that keep the kid indefinitely on the app doing random things instead of helping them focus on executing the tasks assigned by the parent? Talk about a backfire.

title: So Far So Good
body:
If you’re a parent looking for a fun, engaging, and productive way to help your child stay on top of daily tasks and build better habits, the Joon Kid App is a must-try. This app turns to-do lists into an interactive game where kids take care of a virtual pet called a “Doter,” and every real-world task they complete helps their pet grow and thrive.

What I loved:
	•	Gamified Motivation: The game-like approach makes chores and routines exciting. My child actually looks forward to brushing teeth or doing homework just to earn rewards in the app.
	•	Parental Controls: The parent dashboard is easy to use and allows me to assign tasks, monitor progress, and approve completed activities.
	•	Positive Reinforcement: Instead of constant reminders, my child now feels ownership over their daily responsibilities. The app rewards consistency, effort, and good habits.
	•	Educational Angle: It subtly encourages time management, independence, and goal-setting skills.

What could improve:
	•	Some customization options are limited (e.g., not all tasks are editable in detail).
	•	It’s more effective for younger kids (around ages 5-7); older children might find it less appealing.
	•	There’s a subscription cost, which may not work for every family’s budget—but there is a free trial to test it out.

Overall Rating: 4.9/5

Joon isn’t just another kids’ app—it’s a clever way to turn parenting into teamwork. If you’ve struggled to get your child to stick to routines, this might be the help you’ve been looking for.

What I love most is the convenience: I can edit everything from my phone, and my child can check off tasks and earn rewards directly on his iPad. It’s super easy to use and makes accountability fun. Highly recommend!

title: A game changer for our family!
body: I had been skeptical and did the 7 day trial but was blown away by the immediate effect Joon had on our son! We had become accustomed to being the daily broken record of reminding him to do his daily chores, getting ready for the day, and helping out around the house - often times either being ignored or having things escalate to push-back and attitude. We added these “chores” as “Quests” into the Joon app, and IMMEDIATELY the game changed. Our son woke up BEFORE HIS ALARM to get started on his Joon quests on Day 2…and excitedly tells us all about his levels and adventures within the app. He does the ‘extra’ quests we’ve added in - in order to earn more tablet time or other incentives, and we haven’t had to remind him about any of his mandatory quests for going on two weeks now! This child who wouldn’t make his bed without a stink now makes his bed and his lunch each day without even a mention - along with a whole host of other helpful things around the house. He’s had a better attitude with his little sister too - helping her navigate the app and earn coins as well. We have quickly determined that Joon was just what we needed to add motivation and fun to the process - and it has made our lives as parents so much smoother each morning and night! Thank you, Joon! We’ve signed up for the yearly subscription.

title: Supporting consistency and exec functioning, lowering anxiety around basic tasks
body:
We are a week in and seeing some nice improvements with our 12 yr old son by using this app.  We already have a rule that tasks need to get done to earn screen time, however, when it’s just a verbal list coming from a parent, sometimes it’s fine and other times it’s challenging.  This app makes it much easier and fact based.  Our son is visually seeing the connection between completing the tasks, seeing the coins he has redeemed and then redeeming them for screen-time.  

The app is a bit tedious to set up.  It took us a few days to think through the values for each task but once we got it set up, it’s really easy.  

The consistency is helpful for our son and we are noticing that sometimes it even helps us remember a task that we would have forgotten (like putting on deodorant!)

 Enhancement request:  the parent app doesn’t let you see the child’s point balance they have earned.  You only see when the child logs into into their companion app to redeem.  I would like to see where they are as we go.

Overall really happy and recommend it!!!

body: We’ve been struggling with routines & losing our minds with repeated instructions. Joon has given our 7 year old a map to independence.
author: Grpapel

title: Chores no longer a chore
body: My kids are more willing for to do ever day tasks without the complaining
author: KylosT

title: ENCOURAGING, METHODICAL, PERSONALIZED CARE.
body: Jennifer W. has been amazing so far. Highly recommend this app and I have only had one session. I have access to our therapist via the apps care chat at all times - business hours apply of course. However, if there is crisis moment where you need help/guidance immediately, you may ask for that and the therapist will make the time to come to you and your child’s aid. Highly recommend. Answer to prayer so far!!
author: JMandJC

title: Lots of Great Features
body:
Pros: 1. Complete personalization of the “quests” I set up for my child to complete (title, image, skill association, mandatory/not, difficulty level, recurrence, time of day, timers, parental review/none, ability to save as template) 2. Complete personalization of rewards (set prices for purchased items or activities, currency exchange for allowance or screen time) 3. Ability to send bonuses when my child goes above and beyond 4. Ability to add & manage more than one child 5. Ability to send in-app messages to child 6. Progress reports in a data dashboard 7. Game play controls 8. Ability to print task charts from the app with all your child’s quests listed
Cons: The age rating starts at 4yo, which I agree with for the quests part of the app BUT the game part of the app is way too complicated for a 4 year old.  I wish they had a simplified user interface for littles
author: DaynBing

title: This works!
body:
Very thankful for the Joon app.  We’ve been using Joon for a month and have seen vast improve in our 3 children (ages 6 through 9) and in us as parents.  Both my neurotypical and neurodiverse children are thriving in their daily routines due in large part to our use of Joon.  

As my children complete tasks (both daily routines and chores) and earn coins, I’m personally rewarded with a sense of peace and a bit of rest.  I no longer have to keep track of who does what, is it fair, when last did I ask them to do a task.  It’s all tracked and monitored by us in Joon.  I now have space in my mind to be present with my family.  My children have commented that I’m not as stressed as I was pre-Joon. 

Give Join a try.  Your family might thrive as a result of this simple motivational tool. 

Do head caution to also include rewards (they can buy with the coins they earn) which don’t cost you money.  Initially, we were spending money on cash or toys that they kept earning time and time again.  We wised up and added rewards to buy “play time” on things such as video games or iPad, etc.  Now our outlay of funds is minimal.  

Note:  you will want to pay the subscription fee so that your family can accomplish even more tasks rather than the limited number of tasks (quests) available in the free version.
author: praylovegrace

title: Works amazing for my kids
body: This is the kind of motivation my kids need to do their tasks and enjoy them.
author: Great For Discounts

title: AMAZING
body: We’ve been using this app for a little over a week and my kids (8,6,4) all LOVE it. It has completely changed our dynamic — I no longer have to remind them constantly of what they need to do, the app does it! We use it on our iPad and the audio feature that reads the tasks out loud is amazing for my kiddo who can’t read yet. My kids literally ask me what else they can do around the house now! Love love love this app!
author: BusyMomYo

title: A Must-Have for ADHD Families
body:
I cannot speak highly enough of this app! As a parent of two kids with ADHD, finding tools that can help them develop independence and structure has been a game-changer. This app has truly transformed our daily routines. 

Not only has it been great for their routines, but it’s also helped them with replacement behaviors. The app provides motivation for them to choose alternative actions when they're feeling overwhelmed,  distracted or frustrated. 

I would recommend this app to any parent with kids who have ADHD—it’s been a true lifesaver!
author: sel2332

title: The Best Thing We Could’ve Ever Done!!!!
body: I love this app, I don’t have a kid myself, but I was added to the group for my niece, and she has been doing absolutely amazing with this, she LOVES her part, and even completes the optional side quests we give her (there are 3-a silly dance party, read a book for 30 minutes and 1 hr of no screen time) she really struggles with completing her responsibilities so this is great for her to come back and reference and double check so she can keep track. setting the expectations and her responsibilities with this has been SO much easier, and there are very few things she has to ask about and clearly define because we can just add it in there where she can see it herself😍 being able to make it to where she needs to give a picture for proof it’s done appropriately and have an area where she can tell us what she had difficulty remembering or doing by herself so we can help her and adjust as we go along is just about the best thing we could’ve hoped for!!!! 100/10 if I could give Joon more stars, I would no hesitation.
author: amoréé

title: Worth it!
body: ASD/ADHD mom here. I downloaded Joon off a Facebook ad I had been seeing over and over. Figured I would just use the free version and hope it helped my 6 year old get going in his morning routine and some other behaviors without the constant arguing we had. 5 days in and I was sold! I bought the full version with the help of the creators offering a discount due to financial constraints. My 6 year old is hooked and getting his daily tasks done with 95% less arguing! We are even potty training with it! My favorite feature is the read aloud. Anytime in the game there is text you have to read, a speaker icon is next to it for the younger kids who cannot read themselves. The independence provided by just that feature alone is amazing! If you’re on the fence, buy it! & 5 stars alone just for the personal help from the creators who are doing all they can to help families like mine
author: Brittany.mikaela

title: Great app
body: My older boys absolutely love this app! They have been doing more around the house even with not fighting with sibling option you have it’s helped their moods so much that I can’t wait to use it with my 6yo soon! Well worth the money in my books!
author: Mamabearx392

title: Love this app!
body: Joon has helped my daughter and I to get on the same page when it comes to chores, learning and physical activities.  My daughter likes playing the game and growing her animal.  This is a great app!
author: prisLopez7

title: No more wars!
body:
I was very skeptical of gamification of every day tasks like Taking a Bath, Make Your Bed, Go to bed without a fuss, etc but it 100% works. 

Instead of taking things away, this is rewards for good behavior and has given some stability back to the household and is SO WORTH the cost.
author: John evv

title: 8 and 10 year old
body:
They use this and it has been helpful for everyone! My 10 year old is watching me type this and said he has been having fun the last couple days and likes feeding his pet. 

My eight year old just loves everything about it. It also makes mornings and afternoons much easier as we don’t need to remind them so much. 

Worth the money for my sanity haha!
author: Tmus1

title: Complete new family
body: I would give this app 100 stars if I could. My family is like a whole new family since this app!! I went from multiple reminders to my kids to not having to even tell them what they need to do! They love completing their quests and earning points to grow their “dinosaurs”! I have a daughter with ADHD and this has been a game changer. She is so motivated!! Take the time to build out your quests (tasks) and it will save you a lifetime of hassle.
author: HL - WI

title: Worth the money
body: I’ve seen several reviews talking about price. My family paid 50 & when you break that down to what it would cost monthly it’s not terrible at all. Now to the app. We use this primarily for my daughter’s morning routine. Prior to using this app every morning was a fight. I would be frustrated at having to repeat myself over and over. My daughter would get angry at my requests. Insert Joon! We did the free trial for a few days and it completely changed our mornings. Now I place the iPad with her morning tasks on her desk and gently wake her up. She completes them on her own and then gets to play with her animal while she eats breakfast. One of my favorite features is you can request a photo for validation of a task. My kiddo loves taking a photo of her clean room every day. We are a homeschooling family so we may apply it more to our days in the future. I love how customizable the tasks can be. She loves not feeling like I’m constantly nagging her to get things done. It’s been such a relief for our mornings. Thanks Joon!
author: TheCenterFamily

title: My kids love it!
body: Great if you need help getting more involved and building positive habits with distracted kiddos, but you do have to invest the time and be consistent as a parent keeping your promises and delivering on the rewards. Still, this has been a great way to help me build positivity with my kids when I’m often busy working or surviving in an overly demanding world. Best of luck!
author: dontforcemetorate

title: Fantastic routine program!
body: My kids always complained how many times I’d repeat myself to get chores done, so I found Joon and won’t look back! My kids are actually doing more and more complicated chores without arguing. Currently they’re only earning the free coins through the app but you do have the option to give other types of rewards. Your family needs this app to help with routine!

title: Wow

author: mazzholler

author: Lacyjay87

title: Joon App 5 Star Rating
body: This app has been a God send to our family. This past week has been amazing. Chores, schoolwork and behavior has been positively changing all week. More ambitious to get stuff done around the house, less complaining from the kids. Let’s not forget to mention the stress load of everything being on my plate has diminished tremendously. I’ll definitely be staying with Joon for my 4 kids.

title: Finally
body: There’s not longer fighting or arguing
author: Kaismom12

title: Makes all the Difference
body: I’m a mama of two ADHD kiddos (9F and 12M) and we have tried everything to make chores and kindness a part of our daily routine eg visual schedules, index cards, timers, other apps…. Having ADHD myself the consistency on my part and the lack of buy-in from the kids have left us with lots of frustration and little progress.   Joon works. The kids do it without complaining and often without being asked. The kids like it and are having fun earning rewards in real life, like time with parents, screen time, actual money…. The initial set up was time consuming but straightforward and now we are cruising! Thank you!
author: pnwmamma

title: Instant success for ADHD child!!!!
body:
This tool has been the first true solution to help our ADHD child end the arguing and forgetting, to now find daily wins over her chores and responsibilities. She LOVES it and is eager to check off all her daily tasks to earn points for her game and buy rewards from a list we designed together. 
The app is also intuitive and easy for a not-too-techy mom to manage and enjoy working with. I’ve already recommended it to a friend and two therapists and several teachers.
author: Momma of ADHD kiddo

title: Overpriced and not worth it
body: Short trial time that doesn’t provide enough time to gauge if your kids likes it or not and super expensive-you’ve already payed a full year of $80 when you realize you just threw your money down the drain
author: Andreinoe

title: Great even for older teens
body: I tried other apps and nothing worked for us, including the prepaid Visa card chore apps. My kids are 16 and 19, both with AuDHD… I was skeptical that they would find this interesting, given that they have steam accounts full of games that they love. However, we got the app this morning and they have been played on it for 5 hours now, in between excitedly doing chores (“quests”). We homeschool, so I added quests for their extra curricular activities.. and they started practicing Spanish and music without being asked. All of their chores were done as if they were playing a game- they had fun washing dishes and handling trash, joking and being competitive for “coins”. This app is magical. I subscribed. It’s also seemingly glitch-free; the developers and design team have done an incredible job.
author: Lznui

title: Amazing
body: Entirely different way of parenting my most difficult child-student 9/10 year olds  with repeating things 3-4x was zooming past the other kids on completing tasks - winner winner chicken dinner - I’m SOLD I was tired of repeating myself and yelling.
author: Luvbugbb

title: Success!
body: Honestly, I am really enjoying the app. The kids are pumped about getting chores done in exchange for coins to feed their doters (pets) and of course rewards that I create. A simple concept that all families can understand and continue to use. I also love that I can ANYTHING into a quest, as simple as brush your teeth to being kind and respectful all day. Customizing the amount of coins depending on difficulty of the task is also great! Looking forward to our continued success with this app!
author: Jennymobile

title: Gamechanger
body: The Joon app and game have made things more fun and enjoyable for my whole family.  Our kids especially those who struggle with executive function have become more self-confident as they execute their daily tasks and goals independently with rewards.  Thank you for creating this app!

body: Our family joined Joon to help us accomplish chores without nagging and arguments.  The tool is easy to use and motivates our children.

author: Ginjared

title: Not for my family
body:
I thought this app would help motivate my children to want to do their chores around the house. It had the opposite effect. My children get minimal screen (tablet/phone) time. So offering the Joon game on my phone actually just caused tantrums and arguments between my children. 
I would love to see another simpler app but with minimal play time. Maybe the ability to buy cute outfits/items. But all the extra “bells and whistles” ending up just overstimulating my children. 
This app might be great if your child has a tablet/phone. But didn’t suit our family.
author: PNWrmama

title: Helpful to our family
body: My oldest daughter has some behavioral challenges and my youngest daughter has focus issues. Joon has been so helpful in encouraging them to complete non preferred tasks in order to earn tokens for rewards. The rewards are chosen by the parent. This is helpful for us, because we can make these rewards positive experiences rather than materialistic items. My daughters have made so much progress just within the past week.
author: Sitcom.Mom

title: Totally turned our days around!
body: My daughter has AuADHD and loves to justify and argue her way out of every direction given. Since starting Joon I have not had to remind her to complete any of the tasks she’s been given!
author: Momaloha808

title: Great app
body: I have two kids. One 7 year old and one 5 year old. My 5 year old struggles to focus and this game has helped him structure his day and help ease with transitions between activities. If you’re looking for something to help, try it out!
author: Father of two in Ca

title: A Smart Tool For Families
body:
Our kids don’t have ADHD or ODD (I don’t even know what that is). 

We use this app to help motivate and remind them of their daily tasks.  My son (8) has really taken to it and has added several tasks and rewards that he is constantly working towards. 

We added big rewards like Late Night Game Sesh With Dad and Ice Cream Date with Mom, they are really excited to hit those goals. 

The entire reason I got the app is because I wanted to “gamify” stats for my son.  We are big gamers and  I often explain his attributes by the way of leveling up his character and skill points.  I wish the app had more of that, even if I am the one manually upgrading his “stats” I think it would be a cool way for him to see and feel progress.  

I would love to see them introduce something like this.

The game part of the app seems to work to keep my kids engaged in the process.
author: CrushMode

title: This app is really helping my daughter!
body: My daughter struggles with separation anxiety on school days that can make it hard for her to get out the door. I downloaded this app over winter break to help with a new morning routine and it’s been working great for us. She thinks the characters are cute and is excited to do her quests to earn coins and play in the game world. Not having to nag her about her tasks has helped everyone’s attitudes and she’s proud to more independently get stuff done. It’s only been a week but she’s consistently using the app each day and  it’s been just the distraction we needed to keep her anxiety at bay and have calm mornings.

author: CJStone23

author: BethanyJ-W

body: This app is amazing! It has not only helped me stay organized, but also my kids. They actually want to do chores and extra activities to earn coins. I can see them trying hard to have better behaviors as well!
author: Mom of 3 with ADHD

title: Couldn’t be happier
body: Its made every day tasks easier for my son to tackle and it’s been so heartwarming to see how satisfied he feels when completing his tasks. I’m excited to see how this impacts his self-esteem as time goes on.
author: LawrenM

title: Upgrade ruined it
body: A previous version made it so the app kept running while kids completed quests. The update made it so the tablet kept turning off (and stopping the timer) unless my son touched the tablet every 30 seconds. It’s completely useless, and a regular timer worked better. Don’t waste your money unless they correct this.
author: Chicken-Burrito

title: We love Joon!
body: Our 3.5 year old son had grown so much since using Joon! He’s doing things happily that he used to fight me on daily. We’re so proud of him and he’s proud of himself too.
author: shaelyn.r

title: Noelle
body: Joon is the best app a parent can have, my children have actually started doing there chores for a change!
author: Palo Alto resy

title: Game changer
body: If you consistently work with your child, they’ll consistently succeed with Joon. Of course kids figure out how to try to get away with not doing any chores and quickly figure out that Joon gets them to do work, BUT I set rewards with my kids and make it so they can see the success and want more! Joon has helped me set more of a routine for my kids, which has in turn helped me stick to more routine as well, and has helped us accomplish chores around the house and a lot of really enjoyable family time! My kids look forward to the new things they can earn for their dotors “for free” so they can save their points for things in real life. It’s also helped them really apply the value of saving and watching what you spend. My my kids say, “please and thank you” with a huge grin on their face after asking for something because they know that’s one of the easy ways to earn some coins. It’s gotten my 7 year old to focus and accomplish goals like no other, even cleaning the litter box, which was always a complete no go before. Also, my kids ask to read to earn more points, when reading time was always a huge argument for my 9 year old. Thank you Joon!! This has been great!!
author: Beans2221w

title: Love the app hate the social aspect
body: Was unaware that there was a social media aspect to this app and feel that is a disappointment. Maybe they will change it or make it so you can turn it off but I bought this to have as a stand alone game that incorporated the tasks that need completing. That would have been enough.
author: sweetwaterdevo

title: Very helpful app
body: I wasn’t sure if this app would work for my child and I was hesitant to pay for a full year without seeing how she responds. Their support hooked me up with a month to month option which I greatly appreciate. So far my child loves the app and it’s helping her establish a routine. Crossing my fingers she stays interested long term. I can set up a variety of rewards that she can achieve. This week she earned an ice cream cone at the store. So far so good.
author: Jennifer Phillips808

title: Absolutely worth it!
body: Very motivating for my 8 year old with ADHD. The immediate positive feedback for completing daily responsibilities is exactly what he needed and it’s building his self confidence.
author: JessicaOman

title: Fun and motivating
body: Our kids are 12 and 11 years old and are enjoying completing their daily quests. This helps them visual and remember their daily routine and to be reminded of their progress. I was able to set up the app in an afternoon with quests that were relevant for us. We’ve been using it consistently for two weeks and I look forward to seeing what more we can do to keep it interesting for them.
author: partypatty.xo

title: Great so far
body:
So far, my son loves it. He has been doing things around the house ranging from playing outside for 30 mins, to chores, homework (without my asking), or just simply getting up and dressed without a fit. These are all to earn coins to buy food and toys for “Wilchy”, his pet dotor. It’s essentially a tamagotchi that he has to keep alive by doing things around the house, things that are good for him or just being helpful - my son has cooked dinner with me TWICE!

We had one fit within the last week and it turned out he had been bullied at school and had a lot of emotions to let out, not because of the task (taekwondo class). This is a huge improvement from everyday melt downs about simple things like putting on pants or putting away toys.

I’m still just dumbfounded that something so simple has worked where chores charts, punishments or anything else has not.
author: Eolaf22

title: Great for Consistency for All Family Members but at a Price
body: I use this app with my family and it helps us to stay on top of tasks, schedule to do lists, and make tasks that were once impossible into something my kid is more eager to complete. He says homework and chores feel more like a game and a challenge for him, and he is very happy. Just be aware of the price of the service from the start. It’s an investment, but if the app proves valuable to you and your family like it does for mine, the $12.99 monthly or $89.99 yearly is more than worth it.
author: Mandiiroo

title: Love this app
body: I have one 16 year old autistic daughter and 2 other children (8,11)who all use this app. All three of them love it. I gave the free trial a go and it made a big difference in our home. Instead of me just getting mad, this was a practical and fun ways to get us all on the same page. I made some family challenges like playing a board game with mom (their choice of game), going to a movie and getting ice cream. Now they are all in serious conversations with each other about how to earn these rewards. It’s fun to watch them care about chores now. Thanks joon!

title: The best
body: Great app that has had such a positive impact on my family. Hoping  it continues to motivate my kids to stick to their routines.
author: Dnie11e

body: You do need to set it up in a way that works for your family. But once it is set up, it works perfectly! Been keeping my kiddo on track!

author: ItsReign

author: sugarmarievintage
