body:
First day!  Her Doter, Nostradamus, is 0 days old still and appreciation for the joy and motivation she is experiencing with the Quests is through the roof.

Such a great game.  Delivers exactly what it intended.  

I am excited to see her progress.
author: I paid. You did not deliver.

title: My kids love it
body: This app is great.  Just what my family needed.  It’s taken the fight out of daily routines and allowed my kids to tangibly see good choices adding up.  I’ve seen great progress
author: berrymkg

title: We love it!
body: This has helped quite a bit with routines and goal setting in general. It does take some set up initially but it is WORTH it! Customize to every kid in the family and it’s FUN!
author: Emmetts

title: Love this app!
body: This app has been create for helping my daughter with ADHD and some executive functioning issues establish some routines and alleviate the load me too!!  Highly recommend!
author: Lillian Jurjovec

title: Going great - excellent customer service
body: Joon was going *so well* for our neurodivergent family - changing the tone of our home, freeing up time for relationship rather than task management and meltdowns. A week into it, however, the app wouldn't work without a required update. We did the update and the app crashed every time we opened it. It was incredibly frustrating - especially since we are paying $90 a year for this app. After writing the customer service team through the “contact us” form in the app, I heard back within a day and they worked with me for several days straight until the issue was resolved. They were kind and attentive, enlisting the engineers to fix whatever problem had occurred on their end. We got it all sorted!
author: Lyda the great

title: Game Changer!
body: I was surprised by the 1-star reviews for this app. Despite the $90 yearly subscription, I believe it’s worth it as a dedicated mom. With two of my four children diagnosed with ADHD, this app has greatly improved their behavio, focus and motivation. Our mornings before school are much better now, thanks to our consistent use over two weeks. It has eased my stress and reaffirmed my decision to seek out behavioral tools. I'm truly grateful for this experience.
author: Mom_Four

title: NOT FREE
body: The ad said the add is free, it is $90/year. But you find it out after wasting your time creating a profile and answering a ton of questions
author: Yuli Zlen

title: Motivating!
body: My kids age 9 and 12 both love it and enjoy completing their jobs each day. They love the pet feature and like earning points to spend on their pet or prizes.
author: LauraD0603

title: So far so good!
body: We have been using it for about a week and my son enjoys earning points, he’s 6 so he doesn’t quite get the caring for an animal yet, but it’s something we can do together!
author: Cahia123

title: It does work!
body: My kid loves it so much! She asks every day if I can afford the upgrade yet! Lol! We are waiting on the therapist to join. The only thing is, during the wait, she gets discouraged cause I can’t approve all her quests. If anyone needs this, it’s definitely my little one. She’s my niece.. her mom passed on her 3rd bday. She had neurofibromatosis, which caused cancer. My little has the NF1 as well, along with Asd and adhd… and a sad dad… who lets her do life with the screen in her face :( so it’s a struggle. But she loves this app! I just wish she had more games that would give her points, or coins for being AFK (away from keyboard) cause that WORKS TOO!! Lol! Thanks for an awesome change with this app;)
author: jbirdjones81

title: This works!
body:
This works if you really stick with it for your kids. 
This is the only review I have ever given for an app because I feel this is a game changer.
author: NinaBDel

title: Helping us with using our Back Brace! And many other hard things!
body: We are really enjoying using Joon to grow and dress and feed our cute little animals over here- all with Mom really getting the benefit of kids excited to do hard things! My daughter has Early Onset Scoliosis and has to wear a full back brace 18 hours a day. She struggles greatly with motivation to do this. We are also using it for chores and self care tasks with great success for both of our youngest daughters!
author: EmilyStrawberryPiper

title: Scammy at best
body: I got lured in by the “free trial”. But I couldn’t login for the first 4-5 days, every time I requested to reset password it would not work, and then when I finally got in I didn’t have time to use it before they charged me for the FULL YEAR SUBSCRIPTION without any notice.
author: Oldskoolbookfan

title: Has helped keep my daughter on task
body: This app has really helped my daughter stay focused on specific tasks. We don't get every task done but she understands more each day what her routine is and which ones she should be prioritizing. They also love the piggy bank and earning coins!
author: senycewhite

title: Great for Teens too!
body: My 14 and 17 year old are using this app - it’s cutting down on lots of “reminders” from me. Because they are older, I involved them in helping choose their daily and weekly tasks and asked them to try it during the trial period and let me know if they thought it was helpful. They liked it- my younger teen especially likes the rewards she can earn IRL and says she finds that very motivating. So glad this app exists!
author: QualitySeeker2024

title: Excellent App
body: We have found this to be such a joyful and collaborative way to engage our children and they have showed both motivation and positive growth. We are so grateful!
author: Solandes77

title: Misleading
body: I spent 15 mins answering all the questions and setting up the profile just to find out that it costs $120/year. Nope! So I gave you all my info and now I can’t even use the service unless I pay this outrageous amount!
author: BECKS-2000

title: Great tool for all three kids!
body: I love that the kids are motivated to complete their tasks and that it’s a place to keep track (with three kids!) so they can see how much more points they need to reach a reward.
author: Amanda415xox

title: Game Changer in our Household!
body: I have two kiddos on the spectrum and the daily chore and personal care grind has been a major PITA, until we discovered Joon. We’ve been using it for only two weeks and the entire atmosphere in our home around daily responsibilities has completely changed. My older kiddo isn’t as into the game portion, but that’s totally fine. The reminders on his phone are all he needed and this app provides that in spades. I didn’t want to juggle multiple chore apps and this way I don’t have to. My teen daughter absolutely LOVES the game portion. She is obsessed with updating and leveling up her doters and I love her enthusiasm! I never imagined that I’d be able to find an app that tackles these issues and also make it fun, but this one does! I only wish we had found Joon sooner.
author: rotabega

title: Ditch the Charts.. & Threats- Joon Works!
body: After creating, trying and never following through on many ways to make our mornings better- It’s been about a month with Joon and my kids have cashed in rewards and we get out the door on time! I was able to get the cost reimbursed by some local waiver funds. It’s great to have an app designed with ADHD in mind!! Thank you Joon.
author: TheresAnApp4Thaaa

title: Scam
body: Repeatedly tried to cancel subscription and  i am still getting daily withdrawal attempts!!! Impossible to cancel and communicate with this “company”!!!!
author: Farrahpp

title: No more tears!
body: Motivates the kiddos to complete their routines. My kids run to check Joon as soon as they wake up to start checking off tasks and see how their little pets have evolved. The kids no longer see me as nagging them to get things done.
author: Topsytail

title: My kids love this!
body: This is super affective. I have a third grader and second grader, and they are doing more great things around the house on their own because of the app. Rewards really motivate some kids, and that ADHD brain really lights up with this app!
author: EmilyHirse

title: Great for building routine and homeschool
body: My 8 year old daughter has trouble staying on task and staying motivated. This app has helped our relationship, because now we aren’t in a power struggle everyday. The coins and animals she takes care of on the app motivate her to get herself dressed in the morning and complete all her school work. I also appreciate how you can tailor the goals to your family’s needs. Great app!
author: summergilly

title: So helpful
body:
We are a neurodivergent family and this has really helped my kiddos to stay on task. It’s also helped me to stay on top of keeping them accountable, since they ask every day for me to check their chores and approve them. 
The animals are so cute and remind me of tamogotchis (though with more features and fun things to do.)
Highly recommend for other families that struggle with routines!
author: Suki scj

body:
Join has made a huge impact in my sons life 
He has high functioning adhd and has a hard Time with routine and self control and join has help him so much in thinking things through and helping build better habits for himself we love it
author: You shaved

title: Doesn’t motivate kids to do their assigned task
body: This app doesn’t motivate kids to do their daily tasks, the only thing my kids wanted to do was play the game. Rather than do their jobs, they would choose to not be in the app. I don’t like that this app encourages more digital game time.
author: A.l.Hahn

title: Great positive motivation!
body: Great app for positive motivation and rewards! Customizable quests and rewards allow you to make it meaningful to your situation.
author: Kalyn*O

title: Such a great motivator
body: This app has helped my son with ADHD to stay on task and accomplish goals. It has helped my younger son learn responsibilities. It has helped me to yell less! 😆 I couldn’t be happier with it and find it to be completely worth it.
author: LMHooker

title: Really motivated our kids
body: Our kids have always had chores but we were finding it hard to motivate them and get them to do the chores without being reminded all the time. We really liked the Joon app for ease of use and the kids have been really excited hatching Doters and taking care of them. They have fun saving up coins to use for rewards I have set for them also. I would definitely recommend this app to other parents. It still surprises me when I get up and they have already made their beds for the day without being asked.
author: MElias243

title: Keeps my child motivated in a fun (and easily manageable way)!
body:
We’re loving Joon and calling it our latest parenting win! Our son is hard to motivate and gets bored after awhile of “new” charts and reward systems. We’re trying to empower him to be responsible for his own health/hygiene, and a few small chores around the house. With Joon we sat down together to talk about responsibilities, timing expectations, and fair rewards. He thinks the pet theme is fun, and even spends some of his quest coins on changing colors and buying props. 

We also talked about the “cashing in” of his coins. He loves that he has a larger goal to work towards and can get rewards even outside of the app. 

So far, worth every penny!
author: Lynzeeeee

title: The perfect ADHD app!
body:
Me and my kids (3,5,10) have been using this app for a couple months, and we all love it! I have ADHD along with my two older kiddos. I even created me a profile, I’ve use many apps to try and get more organized and motivated, none have done what Joon has!! I love the “anytime” section, and all chores go there, I don’t “have” to schedule a chore on specific days which was the major problem with other apps. And they don’t have the rewards and cute creatures like Joon! 
I have set up a basket with rewards they can earn and let me tell you, every day they are asking what else they can do just to get the prize. I took them to the dollar store and let them pick out what they wanted, then it goes to the basket to be bought with their points. 
It also works great on the 3yo, they all get excited for chores😂 
This app is truly a live changer for my family!
author: Katie5614

title: Such a life saver!!
body:
We have 4 kids 3 of them have been using Joon for about 2 weeks and it has been a life saver and a time saver! Their ages range from 13-8 years old and I truly struggled with having to CONSTANTLY remind them of what they should be doing in the morning (brushing teeth, making bed….) what their chores are for the day, and what the should be doing before bed. At first I did have to remind them to Check their task on Joon 😂 but now they just do it on their own !! 
Also really love that I can approve their task or ask them to “retry” them, and I love that I can request a photo! The photo option for PROOF that they actually did the task is a huge time saver and created accountability and independence. Which was our whole goal for trying this app out in the first place.
author: forever sanchez

title: Can I get a refund please
body:
Hi, I used this for several weeks but it wasn’t easy for me or my kids to use. My older kid kept changing the rewards so I couldn’t figure out the setting to lock down that feature. My younger kid was crying because she couldn’t feed her doter or something. For me it was hard to manage and each time I added a chore I had to start from scratch . It just didn’t work for us but I can see how it may work for a different family.
Thanks,
Patrice
author: Patttpat1

title: My kids love it
body: My 3 girls have been loving Joon! They have been doing extra chores to get max points so they can get money for allowance and ice cream dates with me or my husband. I love that we have been able to personalize it so much to our needs.
author: jourdan333

title: Fantastic Behavior motivation app for autism adhd kid
body: This is so worth the money for this app!  My son likes the game, he’s motivated to actually do his quests in the game to earn coins , I can create or use templates it’s user friendly, I can’t brag about it enough.  If you knew my son and how he would not do what he’s supposed to, and we have tried many things nothing worked.  He can save up for a night out to the movies.   Must check out the free trial, you will not be disappointed I promise you.   Especially if you have a kiddo that is good in school and comes home and falls apart.  Angel in school Devil at home.  lol.   TY Joon!   Grateful for the win!
author: Coush01

title: Unique & fun motivation for an anti-chore/task kiddo!!
body: I’ve finally found something that makes it fun for my kiddo to complete tasks (everything from doing homework & getting ready for the next day/getting ready in the morning to cleaning her room and doing chores)…. I feel like I’ve tried just about everything, positive and consequence enforced, I was exhausted from the constant nagging. My kiddo is not a very motivated individual- either she WANTS to do it, or she simply will not. This app was suggested to try and I’m very pleasantly surprised at how it’s changed EVERYTHING. She loves the games on the app and loves completing her “quests”… I like how easy it is to assign everything, from a schedule to tasks on certain days, I can make it so she has to upload a picture to “show” a task is completed (she loves these!). I haven’t even completely explored all the aspects of the app but so far, we BOTH love it!
author: hope♥

title: Will update with more use
body:
••Day 6. Still 4 stars. 9.16.24 Well. My 9 year old ran away from home today. so clearly we’re winning around here. Will begin again tomorrow. Also of note, my free trial ended today and my one month subscription starts. 

•• Day 2. Still 4 stars 9.12.24 Today was a little bit of a disaster but still a good day and better than where we started. PROS- my oldest is a check list kid so he got started immediately this morning and was excited to do his quests. -I discovered today how to tell the difference between a mandatory and optional quest (purple ring around the quests are mandatory) I wish that fact had been more obvious. - I was frustrated at first because a task my oldest had been putting off all summer I put on the quest list as optional. Since he is a check list kid he finally completed it. But it reappeared the next day! I figured out I had set the interval to repeat daily instead of does not repeat. BUT I thought does not repeat meant it wouldn’t show again. UNTRUE! It stays on the list until it’s completed then falls off. So I’m happy about that. - my boys are super motivated to get more creatures so that’s fun. I added some real life rewards that my boys are excited about. -over all my micromanaging and resulting mental exhaustion over the past 2 days has decreased and there seems to be an overall aire of not so much tension. -your avatar can send messages. Whatever you want to the individual child and my boys seem to be really loving that. CONS- my youngest likes to just interact with the creature. However and this is a *PRO here you can set time limits/restrictions. So until he gets the quests done he can’t take care of the creature. Unfortunately this has lessened the motivation for him. - TIME I don’t know if it is because it’s new or my youngest is just playing or having to read, do, check off, move to the next start again and so on or what but man the beat of the day has slowed!! Although maybe it’s a PRO because even though me tailing them is ‘faster’ it’s not better or easier on me. -TIME, this one is a tricky one. I am spending a HUGE increase in time on my phone for the this app. The results are speaking for themselves so it’s hard to label this as a con but I’m busy. I don’t have excess time to be lallygagging on my phone. Plus it’s weird that I’m ‘spending time’ with my children who are right next to me THROUGH an electronic device. But again. Less tension. Plus this really can’t be helped because if you want the program to run… you, have to run it… Anyway. As of today I decided to buy one month worth. 12.99/1 month so I could really give it a try. Will update again. So I’m in my trial period 7 days. I thought I’d write in real time.

•• Background: I have two sons 19 months apart currently 9 and 11. We are using: parent app on Apple iPhone 8 IOS 16.1.1 BOTH children are on Amazon Kindle fire tablet HD10 I was nervous about the Kindle situation but so far no issues. I was able to download it IN ‘Amazon kids’ to each child’s profile with no problem. So far no glitches. *of note I added an EXTRA profile that has longer app time and is awake earlier and longer for the purpose of apps like this. Oldest is AuDHD level 2 twice exceptional Youngest is AuDHD level 2 PAD Day: 1 9.11.2024 if every day were like today then this is heaven on earth. -pros, the interface is easy to use and set up It’s vibrant and well suited to entertain. I feel like it is well suited for what we’re trying to accomplish. I feel like it’s a well designed therapy tool disguised as fun. Once I got started adding quests I found SO MANY to add. -cons so far - the search function is AWFUL. you have to use almost exact wording. Then even if you have the correct wording you have to select which CATEGORY you want to search. Like seriously? I have two autistic sons. I don’t have time for that. So I ended up making mostly just custom tasks (quests) to hasten set up. -edit. Once you have a custom quest set up if you want to edit it the edit options are not the same as set up. So if you edit for one child it may not apply to another child. Again. I don’t have a whole lot of extra time to edit every faucet of a task for each child. It almost becomes easier to delete and start over. That’s all I got for now will update later
author: ajwilli4

title: Beyond exceeded expectations!
body:
I genuinely thought that I was going to give this a try and that it wouldn’t work and I’d delete it. My homeschooled 9 year old has always argued about schoolwork, about chores, bedtime, etc. I decided to create some quests such as “keep a positive attitude today” and “wait until it’s your turn to talk during conversations”. It has EXTREMELY helped him with patience and gratitude, he’s doing homework with minimal, if any arguing, and I got out of the shower one day to him DOING THE DISHES without being asked. He asks me to add more quests on occasion to earn more coins. 
I have nothing but the most positive things to say about this app!
author: KorMag7166

title: Cute and motivating
body:
Joon was suggested to me by a family member and it has been a great way to motivate our kids into completing tasks and allowing them to self judge timing for said tasks. 

Much like a star chart kids get the choice to complete things around the house that you can personalize. For example one of my children has a difficult time with walking up on time so their reward has more value than something that is easier such as putting their clothes in the hamper. 

They get to use their earned coins to decorate their creature’s (dotters) house or dress them up. There is mini games and adventures. They take care of the dotters and earn more.
author: NixPenAndSword

title: Great Behavior Modification App!
body: We have been using this app to get my grandson to do chores, complete H.W., follow a routine, control his behaviors, and many other tasks. So far we have been very pleased with the progress he is making. He in turn gets rewarded with points to go on Quests. This motivates him to want to do more. Thank you for a well-thought out program that works.
author: Jamerie18

title: Great app!
body: We are loving this app and how it’s motivating my child to complete tasks. Building a routine with incentives you can control virtually works great for our family, and for our child. So glad we found this app!
author: Cupcake crystal

title: Terrible app
body: Went to cancel the trial and they still tried to charge me for a full year of service. I haven’t even had a chance to set up my boys accounts
author: Noooope1234

title: Completely worth it!
body: Joon has been so great for our 9 and 11-yr old kids. You can create your chore list and assign a certain number of coins to each chore. They use the coins to get a doter (like a dinosaur/pet/cute thingy). They can feed and dress the doter with things they buy from the store with their coins. They can go to different worlds/lands for each level they pass (depending on how many chores they complete regularly). They can also use the coins to buy screen time instead. I've even added things to the list that aren't chores, but things they need to remember to do, such as "don’t fight with your sibling" or "get sports bag ready for tomorrow", or "brush teeth" and "get PJs on" which can earn special points. My 9-year-old daughter loves to play Joon and the lands that she gets to explore. And my 11-year-old likes to collect the coins to get more screen time. All-in-all, Joon has helped me from feeling like I have to constantly yell to get things done. If they ask for screen time, I simply have to ask if they've completed everything in their Joon list, and wah-la! Also, since we don't allow screen time in the morning, I wrote the list of things for them to do and put it on our refrigerator. Then, when screen time is appropriate after school, then they can mark off their morning chores. It's been a great system!
author: Lady Boss Bulldog

title: Game changer for my ADHD child
body: Honestly, I’d seen the ads before for this app and didn’t think it would work. I didn’t want to pay for it. I finally decided to give it a chance with the trial cause nothing else worked with my ADHD kid anyways. We started off small, but it really has changed his behaviors. He’ll even ask how to get more coins and what can be a quest. Does he always do everything I need him to do perfectly? No. But there is so much less fighting now that it’s been worth every penny.
author: Ggnuke

title: Great app to motivate kids!
body: The Joon app has been very easy to use as a parent, and our child loves completing his tasks so he can take care of his pet. For a child who is difficult to motivate sometimes, and can get distracted easily, this keeps him on track and is teaching valuable time management skills as well.
author: MJWHAT1023

title: Join us a Godsend
body: Joon is an absolute godsend for us! Our 11-year-old twins have jumped right in and love the app as much as I do! Organization has replaced chaos at our house since joining Joon!
author: Mama2TroubleX2

title: Great App!
body: This app is great! My kids love taking care of their “pets”. It makes them switching chores every other week so much easier since I can make the chores change ever other week. I love the flexibility and the excitement that my kids have with finishing their quests. I am so glad that I found this for my family!
author: The Gravis family

title: Awesome app
body: We love this for keeping schedule for our 8 yo
author: sarahd921

title: Changed our house dynamics
body: This apps has been equally amazing for our kids and us parents (yes, we have our own quests!). We have organized morning with little to no si bling rivalry (big issue), we have organized meals where the kids are engaging in communication (a quest to share a good and not so good part of the day - coins for active listening!), we have increased food choices, rooms are clean and organized (they were willing to downsize), we have grown more independent, and share responsibilities. Overall we are a much happier household and the level of stress and chaos has down a lot. The funniest thing is - they have not asked for big rewards, just the positive reinforcement has been enough of a drive. Highly recommend this app!!
author: JCBT86

title: Love it!
body: 2 adhd and strong-willed kids. Saw the ad for this and tried it. They love the game and are motivated! We’ve been using it for a few weeks now and I need to monitor it but it’s something we complete together so adds more bonding time too.
author: liliarebecca

title: Helps motivate my son
body: I downloaded the Joon app about a month ago. My son is definitely more motivated to complete his chores and requires way few reminders which is a huge win. Two suggestions that would make it 5 stars: 1) a parent starter video that gives you an overview of how the parent app works with the child’s app (I was initially confused they are two completely different apps). The video would be great if it showed parents how to build quests but also showed what the child gets to do in their app. 2) There is a screen time limit for the child, but there doesn’t seem to be a way to only limit the gaming portion without also limiting the “checking off chores” version. My son keeps needing more time to use the timer feature for some of his chores when I had set the limit more for him to not play too much time on the game.
author: chase bury

title: Joon!
body: We are loving it and its been 2 weeks only! No more groans when I say chore time! My child redeems for her rewards like activities, sleepovers, or just a sweet treat! She enjoys playing the video game aswell! She has been playing it instead of Roblox! I think more people should try this out because it has different things. Like for example, it has things for behavior, ADHD, ODD, and more! It’s a real game changer if you ask me!
author: Arfi D

title: So Grateful!
body: This app is fantastic! My 8 yo has ADHD and struggles with completing day-to-day tasks without frequent reminders. With Joon his motivation and independence has increased exponentially. He enjoys completing quests and earning the rewards that follow so much I rarely have to remind him to do anything.
author: Emjay1128

title: We love it
body: Me and my son love this app its helped both of us stay on track and motivated !!
author: 444Nova

title: Doesn’t solve everything but it definitely helps!
body:
I’ve been using Joon for about a month now and so far it has been very helpful. The first few days were absolute game changers for my 9 year old kid who really struggles to get through the basics. We think she has PDA for those who also identify there. She loves taking care of her animals and hatching new ones. I really appreciate that the game seems to evolve as the kids use it - I was worried the excitement of a new game would ware off quickly and she’d no longer care about completing her quests. However one month in she is getting more animals and new aspects of the game unlocked so she is still excited. 

There have been days where Joon has been 💯 responsible for getting her to do the majority of her daily activities. Other days she is less motivated, but I’ll take any wins I can get. It really seems to give kids who need external motivation the push they need to do the things they don’t want to do. Chore charts have never worked for us longer than a week or so because the delayed gratification has not been a strong enough motivator. Joon gives my daughter the immediate dopamine hit she needs to push through brushing her teeth, eating her meals, getting dressed, etc. I don’t know how long it will work for us but I’m thankful for every day that it does!
author: Oaklandaj

title: Changes and updates
body: We’ve been using Joon for the last year and my kid has loved it over all but I can’t justify the huge cost to keep it going for another year. Too bad it’s so expensive or we’d continue with it.
author: Kernelkeep

title: Love it
body: Daughter loves it
author: LaRen121

title: Great motivation for my 5 year old
body: My 5 year old is diagnosed with autism and lately we have been struggling with aggressive behavior when it comes to completing tasks such as getting dressed and brushing his teeth. Since starting Joon, he has been so motivated to complete those tasks and so much more. He love taking care of his doter and using his coins to get rewards from mom and dad. Mornings and bedtime have been much smoother since starting Joon.
author: Kelcey0715

title: Great App
body:
It's been almost 2 weeks since we started with Joon and my son's taking ownership of certain responsibilities. It's still a struggle but the app has been extremely helpful.  
It's fun for him!
author: Mariboza73

title: The kids really enjoy it!
body: My kids are loving this app. I appreciate the printed option so my kids can see on paper what their chores are, and they get 10/20mins each day to play with their little creature when chores are completed. The only reason for the four stars is that the app does freeze up with some of the games. Just a few bugs to work out, but a fun app for our family’s productivity!
author: HCasebolt

title: Charged without reminder
body:
I downloaded this app even though it’s almost $100 because it specifically said they’d send reminders about the free trial ending. And of course they didn’t. I should have known and set a reminder myself. Didn’t get a single app notification or a single email. 

My son likes this app just ok. It doesn’t hold his interests that long because there’s not too many things to do. He’s on his second egg, and after feeding etc there’s literally nothing else for him to do. So he don’t really see that much of a reward for completing quests. 

Also, why is this app so expensive? And why isn’t there an option to pay monthly? My guess is that this app is geared towards desperate parents who are at their wits end trying to help their child become functional adults. A week’s long trial meant for children with adhd or autism is not nearly long enough. Even if you got rid of the trial and just have an option for monthly payment that would be fine. But I just paid almost 100$ for an app that my child is already losing interest in after only a week. So. Fun times for me I guess.
author: JamminMufasa

title: Awesome app for our ADHD 11 year old
body: This app is what we finally needed to get our son on track, we’ve tried many other systems but Joon is what finally worked!
author: Hahsiidnvajx

title: Helps kids with chores
body: We have been using Joon for a few weeks and it has been fabulous helping our kids establish a regular routine and get chores done. We love it!
author: Britte

title: It’s helped my daughter with ADHD feel more independent
body: Having a child who struggles to keep a mental checklist, or even a physical checklist on her own, Joon has given her independence in completing daily tasks and she has quickly accumulated coins for her pet and some irl treats. Looking forward to learning more about the app and seeing how it can help keep the peace in our home.
author: Djziwb

title: Great for kids with ADD
body: This is a great tool to use for kids with and without ADD, I have one of each. They are excited to complete their task to earn rewards. My child with ADD independently opens app and completes task without being asked. It is getting her on a schedule/routine and building confidence. I would recommend this app for all children no matter age. I honestly think it would help adults that have ADD as well. Just seeing your daily schedule in front of you and having a check list builds a routine and independence will follow.
author: Great is His works

title: A huge incentive for my daughter
body: My 5 yo daughter with SPD and suspected ASD struggles with completing basic daily tasks & this has been a fun and engaging way for us to journey through the to do list & incentivize daily with something she actually is motivated by. She told me tonight before bed that she wishes planet Joon was real!
author: BrittFlow

title: Wish I downloaded sooner!
body:
I have told all of my friends and family about this app, as well as my children’s teachers. Please give this app a try, you won’t be disappointed. I first discovered this app on an Instagram ad. I rarely ever download too many apps to my phone, but I have no regrets downloading this at all. My children get excited to do tasks, we communicate better without me nagging them (so much fun LOL), and with being able to customize the reward system best fit for your circumstances, you get family time together. I allowed my kids to write down some rewards they would like, and allow them to make that choice, and then it’s up to them to work for those rewards! You can add your own specific tasks and rewards. You can even throw some bonus “just because” coins their way on the very special days! 
Consistency is key, so make sure the app is being used daily 😊

I have never seen my daughters bed made so many days in a row until this app! 😂

Take it from me, at least see if for yourself!
author: VictoriaKling

title: Encourages a positive attitude
body: It changed the energy around doing chores, tasks and physical activity. I can ask the kids to do an unusual task and they immediately negotiate points to feed their pets! It’s working.
author: Rawshaad

title: Great app for neurotypical & neurodivergent kids
body: As a child psychologist, I have high standards for apps and programs that are to be used for behavioral change. I’m happy to report that after using the app with my own three children, I can give a resounding recommendation. The app is engaging to kids, motivating, and easy to use. Not only do kids have the opportunity to earn positive reinforcement through coins in the game, they can also earn and redeem prizes outside the game. Sitting down to review completed quests with my child gives me lots of opportunities to reinforce and praise the kinds of behaviors I want to see improve. Overall, it’s creating opportunities for success.
author: Pedpsych

title: Not just any chore app!
body: This app has saved my life!! It keep the children busy and on task with the quest I’m able to give them! They look forward to being able to not only complete the quest but receive the rewards they’re able to get from completing the quest. I would recommend it to all moms(especially SAHM) it’s very much a breath of fresh air.
author: HannaGS4

title: Game Changer
body:
My son exhibits ADD tendancies and while when he's in the right mindset/mood to listen and obey to basic tasks like getting dressed, he has little to no internal motivation for these tasks so it's often an argument. He loves the gamified approach to daily tasks and is excited to work his way up to real life rewards my husband and I have set for him. He also enjoys 'raising' and taking care of his pets.

My only wish would be that the trial would be longer. It takes longer than 7 days, at least in my household, to get the hang of a new routine/new system. And the initial excitement of something wears off at some point. So I think a 2 week trial would be helpful to allow that initial excitement to dissapate and be able to see if the motivition to use the app continues for the child.
author: Sarah481

title: Transformative app
body: This app has helped create a more peaceful household and has brought such joy to our children. They love playing the games and caring for their doters — and now volunteer and take the initiative to help around the house and take on more independence. I’m sort of shocked by what an app can accomplish!
author: Cactus C Cactus

title: Joon
body: You have to pay a lot of money
author: Moose and Stella

title: A useful tool for boring routines.
body: We gave this a try with our kiddo and it continues to surprise me. The more we use it, the more interested my kid has gotten. Assigning quests is only limited by my imagination and follow through. Gamifying all the tasks we usually fight over has given us some relief thanks to this app. This isn’t a cure for adhd struggles but a seriously helpful tool to reduce the conflict in our household.
author: Jetgirljade

title: Fantastic.
body:
I am an educator, consultant, and a neurodivergent parent of neurodivergent kids. This app is EXACTLY what we needed. I cannot believe the difference in our entire household in a mere 24 hours since “onboarding.” It is designed extremely well for the way both I and my children operate. I am extremely grateful this exists & I hope it will continue to exist. 
* Massive potential for a school-wide version.

One complaint: we need the fire tablets to be able to take photos as our children do not use Apple devices yet. 

Last complaint: the use of “mandatory” is unclear for me. If there is a repeating “mandatory” task - that must be done morning, afternoon, and evening - how can they finish their morning tasks & then have free time - but then again have to complete the afternoon’s mandatory tasks and so on in evening? My assumption is that mandatory “anytime” tasks simply must be done before game time begins? That is also unclear for me.

Comment on Ux: the reminder feature & deadline feature are fantastic. However, it would be more functional if there was a start time/reminder and an end time or due time - as this would also be supportive for developing the executive function skills needed for being in a team project in the future. Right now it is unclear when they will be reminded, and with how much notice. It is also unclear what happens at the actual time a task is due. Will they get an alert? If it is incomplete at that time is it automatically marked as “skip”? This is not a complaint but just a comment on what the “next level” could potentially be for maximally utilizing the potential of this incredible tool. 

Thank you for creating this!

title: Perfect for our ADHD family!
body:
We are loving Joon so far! It’s been great for motivating my kids to self-start, which means I’m asking them to do less and they are less resistant when I do prompt them. 

As a parent with ADHD, it’s been great to keep me a little more organized as well. I love all the customizations so I can change things for my kids different needs. They are 5 and 7 and able to navigate everything on their own for the most part. 

Favorite features are #1: that my non-reading child can push the little buttons and have everything in the app read for him… AMAZING! And so empowering for him to be able to do it himself! 

And #2: the option to have them take a picture of the task that I can review before approving. I can give feedback and compliments without needing to stop my current task or having them wait until I can do that. 

10/10 recommend!!!

author: E_tiana

title: Interactive Change In Behavior!
body: My kids were being lazy after school got out for the summer so I downloaded the app. They seemed interested so I did the trial and set up some mandatory quests (brush teeth, brush hair, eat a decent lunch, clean up after yourself, ect.). By day 3 they were asking for more quests to be added! My 13yo son after a long day said “Oh! Yay! I get to unload the dishwasher when we get home!”. WHAT?! 🤣 It’s Amazing. I recommend the app to everyone I know. It is pricey for what it is but I was desperate and tired of coming home to lazy, grumpy kids, & a house more cluttered than I left it! There are some days when we slack on our quests but only after super slam packed weekends when we are unmanageably exhausted and that’s okay! Just remember to get back in track so you don’t waste your money. The 7 day trial is auto set to a yearly subscription after so be aware or be surprised as I was. That’s really my only complaint so far & hopefully it’s my only. We’ve had the app for a short while now so I hope we can keep it up.
author: SuhBuh

title: Seeking dopamine through fights has changed to doing as much routine as possible to be able to play
body: As anyone know with a child with ADHD/ audhd/ odd ect. You find something that works a little and it doesn’t work for long. This is working so amazing and I’m praying because of all the dopamine rushes it remains working. My child was on a low point, none of our previous tactics were even slightly working. It was the worst I’ve experienced thus far. I went searching for any help and I found this app and the watchminder. The watch helps remind her to check the app and do her routine. And this App makes her want to do them and enjoy doing them in her own so I’m not constantly reminding her or asking her to do them. Keeping her morning routine is the only thing that sets her up for a good day. And this app makes her want to. Being able to care for the animals is great, but the games she gets to play with them are also geared towards her brain and struggles and gives her so many dopamine rushes, she’s stopped doing wrong to try to find it in my reactions. I am crazy grateful for this app. It glitches on occasion, but what doesn’t.

I am confident that this is the app that will help change our lives around for the better. Thank you Joon!!!!

body: While my daughter doesn't share my struggles with ADHD, she has been hungry for the structure I've found challenging to provide. Joon has given me the tool to offer her this much-needed structure, providing a platform where I can create quests once and establish consistent expectations for her. Gone are the days of confusion, mixed messages, and me forgetting to assign her the tougher tasks. Now, the only reminder I need to give her to stay on track is to check Joon (and, of course, to approve her completed tasks so she can earn her coins – she's all over me about those earned coins). It's been a game-changer, not just for me but for our entire household dynamic.

My patients have had nothing but positive feedback regarding the app. As a mental health provider, I am able to give my patients goals and they can be uploaded to the app and then be completed by the patient. title: Wonderful customer service and great program
body: We recently allowed our 5yr old to get a tablet but knew we wanted him to earn tablet time and also needed help organizing and visually seeing his tasks and responsibilities and Joon was the perfect program for that. We were very disappointed when the free trial ended and I searched for other alternatives but there wasn’t any that worked as well for our needs as Joon. The owner of the company reached out and told me about the low income family plan they had and helped set us up quickly and got us rolling again. We are so grateful for the app and assistance to keep it up. My son is having less behaviors and there is a lot more peace within our home since he has been playing and using Joon.  It is definitely worth looking into for all neurodivergent families or families who want to encourage independence and responsibility with their kids and household expectations.

author: CarlyMain123

title: From Unwanting to Wanting More
body:
my son (9) used to hate chores, or really anything that required ongoing mental effort. this app has been the BIGGEST game changer in our house, no lies or gimmicks here just a mom who has tried everything from giving allowance, to proving helpings hands basically everything short from doing it myself. not only has he now grown i believe 7 different kinds Joons, there is mini games within & other little accessories or prizes they can redeem in game! we are still learning all the new things he is able to do but it’s been well worth it for when it comes to managing his responsibilities & keeping him on track 

i want to add that you can have the app for free but the quests your child will be able to complete are limited; (i believe it’s only 7 a day) i’m one of the same when it comes to living on the paycheck to paycheck cycle but honestly the yearly plan for 89.99 was 110% worth it. the change i’ve seen when it comes to my child completing tasks is night & day.

oh, nearly forgot to mention you, as a parent can make your own Joon to talk to your children in game by sending words of affirmation or just a simple i love you; you can review the quests before you complete the quest for them to earn their coins, if you have older children you can even require photos to be submitted in the case of being away from home for proof of completion! 

TDLR; this game is worth every penny it’s asking for. it helps struggling parents like myself who have run out of options when it comes to helping our children grow into responsible older children, the meltdowns have gone from 10 to 2 & he’s asking for MORE chores to earn money for his Joon. please give it a shot, i guarantee you won’t be disappointed.
author: gnbimkkm

title: Necessary for Special Needs!
body: I got this app for my 6 year old autistic daughter who was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes. She has to now get 4 shots a day and was struggling. The coins she earned from taking her insulin shots and chores bought her eggs for new animals as well as special rewards from us. She's obsessed with checking it and always reminding me to approve her chores. Her 8 year old Autistic sister clings to this app to help her stay on track with her routine. It has been a major help for both of them and it's been huge for me being able to breathe and not have to hover and constantly remind them what they are doing.  It even has a speaker button to read the chores to my 6 year old who can't read so she knows whats coming next. GAME CHANGER! I am so grateful for this app.
author: raginghippo535

Its interactive features and gamified approach have motivated him to independently tackle tasks around the house with more enthusiasm and responsibility. Over the years, we have taken numerous approaches to getting our kids to be more consistent with helping out around the house. The amount of arguments we have had about chores, homework, etc. since trying Joon have diminished greatly. I am so thankful to have stumbled upon this app and have shared it with many others.

author: Sir_Tenlee

title: Amazing app!!
body: Amazing app!! There are so many helpful tips for parents that I have really enjoyed learning from. The chores/quests ideas for kids are a great way to get them involved and having fun at the same time. I absolutely love it!
author: Marrdulcee

title: Very motivational for my kids.
body: I have one child with autism, one with ADHD, and one who is neurotypical; all of them love this app! Get it and you won’t regret it!
author: Super_tiff1

title: Recommend with patience and love
body:
I was hesitant to turn to an app to try to motivate my kids to do some of their chores. We've tried it, and although it's not a perfect 100% game changer like the ads I saw showed, I am happy to say that I've seen a huge improvement! We struggled with our kids getting to do things the first time we ask. Joon seemed to provide just the right amount of motivation. It was also a good learning opportunity to show the balance of spending their earned coins for their pets basic needs, and then saving anything leftover for exchanging a real life reward. 

I would encourage other families to at least give it a try and to not be discouraged by the struggles of parenting. Just like adults, the solution might be a little different for each kid and family.
author: deypglez

title: Helpful
body: We have six children still at home, and Joon has proven very helpful in keeping track of many of our daily chores!
author: AdoetteW

author: ksskass

body: My boys are 2&6, and before Joon it was such a struggle to complete our morning/evening routines without constantly nagging. Now, all I have to do is mention their pets and they spring right up! The best part is being able to require that certain quests are completed prior to them being able to access their pets! I do wish there were more games to play, rather than just the 3 (and instructions!) but the app for sure serves its purpose! I’m beyond impressed!
author: SamanthaLynn217

title: FINALLY! Something that WORKS!
body: My son is suddenly so motivated to do the things!! 🙌🏼 It helps me with consistency too.
author: jennifurfly

title: Joon was what my whole family needed!!!
body:
Guys.. I thought the reviews were too much, but it's seriously a life changer for my kids that hate chores! I have 3 kids from 4-9 and We did the free trial for a week to see how it did. I'm now on the monthly plan and we LOVE IT!

They were asking me for more chores so they can get more points for their avatar! 
It doesn't have to be chores either, you can put in brushing teeth, or playing outside without fighting, reading a book before bed, whatever works for your family! 

It has taken the begging and reminding out of chores, and now they can get up and do what needs to be done by looking at the list!

My favorite thing is that it will read the list to the kids that can't read yet! It has a little icon they can click, so they don't have to ask a grown up to read it for them. 

My 4 year old does his daily tasks 100% on his own and loves it! The older ones love it too. They have their own devices they can do their list on, instead of having to log in on my phone. You can use tablets or phones and it's so easy once you get the hang of it. Be patient and try for the whole week, they'll be asking you to do it by the time a few days have passed. 

--I highly recommend the "review task" feature, where they have to take a picture and you approve it. We've had the cutest, and funniest pictures to prove they did their task. You can set rewards, or you can up the coins for certain things they worked hard on! 
Turn notifications on, so you don't have them waiting for approval and coins. It's easy to approve 

Honestly.. It has really help improve the flow of our home, and I'm so thankful for Joon! They get to be more independent and I can focus on things that I need to get done. While giving them lots of praise for what they get done! 🩷
author: Mrs_LauraLopez

title: Helpful and positive app!
body: My family loves Joon. It has helped tremendously with my children’s routine. It is most helpful for my children who have behavior issues such as ODD and ADHD. it helps keep them on track and they really enjoy the rewards and taking care of their animals. I highly recommend this app!
author: TessaaMa

author: bkroog

She actually enjoys doing them because she's a big video gamer so she likes that she gets to take care of her little characters and play games. I also set my partner up as my "child" because he has ADHD and he hasn't forgotten a responsibility since, haha.
author: tillytimeboiz

title: More chores done, less whiny kids
body: This app is definitely helping the kids find the motivation to do those super boring household chores that nobody wants to do!  The other great thing about this app is that I am getting encouragement every day that I use this. They send such nice notes to you through the app when you continue to use and be consistent. I think that’s great because it’s not only the kids who need helping getting stuff done!
author: Musikal Mommie

title: Miracle. Worker.
body: Joon is the first app that I’ve been able to get my son excited to use. We’ve gone from arguing over chores and responsibilities to him begging to spend 5 more minutes working on his task list. My son, 8, loves the app and is excited to complete tasks every day. He loves logging in and seeing his character. He loves that no one has to tell him what to do and that it’s in a format that makes it fun for him to complete tasks. His confidence and our relationship have improved so much just in the 7 day free trial. 10/10 recommend this for families with stubborn or unmotivated kids.
author: SpacedSpoon

title: Not great for multiple kids
body:
This app is an awesome idea but after extensively using S’MoresUp for chores Joon falls short in comparison. 

The chore portion of Joon needs to have way more options as it does not work for multiple kids using it. 

Such as chore rotations so that the kids take turns doing them each month. Currently the only option is to set all kids up with the same chore which makes no since because that chore only needs to be done once in the time interval or the other option is set up just 1 kid with that chore but then they are stuck with the same chores every time. Which leaves you having to go back in every month and change each chore manually so they get to do different things each month. It would be nice if it just automatically rotated. 

Also an option to compete for the chore points as in being able to set all chores up for all the kids and whoever does it first gets the points and then everything starts over again the next month. 

Would also be awesome if the time intervals were daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly. How it is now just doesn’t make any since. 

I wish when apps are made they would take the time to look at other apps. 

This app would be the ultimate app if they would take Cozi Family calendar, S’MoresUp chores, and Joon and put them all together. 

I have been waiting for an all in one option to come out and have yet to see any app take on the challenge.

title: So far, so good!
body:
So we’ve had a little bit of struggle with our little one, getting ready in the morning and at night. So we found this app and we hope it would motivate her to do these things on her own. She definitely enjoys earning coins and feeding her pets. So that part is definitely working. 

She is only 4 1/2 so she might be a little bit young for the app, but so far so good!

author: jennyms0530

title: No more fighting
body: My kids have started tackling their homework and chores without the usual complaining. It has also given us a chance to do more fun things through the rewards as a family.
author: Raising4

title: It truly helps!
body: This app has been a game changer for me. It prevents me constantly hounding my kid to get stuff done. It gives her ownership, incentive, and I’ve seen it create a new kind of responsibility in her! She was resistant at first, but now loves it and stays on me when I forget to approve her quests. Working wonders for our ADHD family over here…thanks Joon! I recommend it to the families I know (as a parent and a teacher!).
author: KeliaE

title: So far so good!
body: It’s been really helpful with motivating my 9 year old son to do his chores. I still have to remind him, but he’s always pretty eager to get them done when he remembers. Im hopeful that with consistency it’ll become more of a normal and he’ll remember on his own. It reminds him of pokemon which he loves, so that is a bonus. I like that we’re able to create our own rewards if we want to also. The one thing that I really do wish was possible on the parent side would be to be able to send notifications for individual/specific chores or something to pop up on his phone as a reminder instead of having to verbally tell him. I feel like, in our situation at least, that would help to reinforce the act of doing them “on his own” better. But overall we’re both very happy so far.
author: muckeyD

title: The motivation they needed!
body: It’s been great to motivate my boys to do their chores. They are actually excited to do them and do them with less prompting.
author: FDPAMc

title: Kids Love It
body:
My children (ages 7, 9, 11) love using the Joon app. I’ve seen a quick turn around in their motivation for hygiene and other activities. I still check in on how they’re doing with their morning or evening tasks, but there’s a lot less repetition (nagging) from me. I’d much rather spend time with my kids on a puzzle or reading together, and Joon has helped with that.

Some of the kids ask to have more quests added to help with their progress. “Mom, can you add putting on deodorant for me?” It’s nice that they’re coming up with their own tasks and that I can easily add them through the app. I’ve also noted that their hygiene is better when they’re at there dad’s house for a week. This is great for consistency for dual household kids.
author: MasonHawk5

title: What a gift!
body: This is an amazing solution for kids who need reward systems and stimulation to get through mundane tasks. It really takes the pressure off me and makes it all a collaborative game!  Thank you Joon!
author: Annabritta

title: Worth it!!
body: I kept seeing this pop up on IG and FB. I have ADHD myself and struggle with routine so it’s hard for me to get my kids into a routine when I can barely get myself in one. I downloaded today and did the free trial figure we’ll see how it goes… my kid has been home from school for an hour and has already done so many chores! This is seriously magic and makes it fun for them to help out and get into a consistent schedule. Worth the money. And will definitely NOT be cancelling after the free trial. Like serious. GAME CHANGER.
author: ThrillVanill

title: Meaningful Motivation
body: I started using this app with my 7 year old daughter  to boost her sense of independence and within days she was using it from morning to evening. She loves taking care of her 'pets' and together we think up meaningful rewards that she can earn from showing independent and respectful behavior.
author: Mama2816

title: Great for all ages
body: We’ve been loving, using the app to encourage chores, playtime, and even the kids getting along. I love being able to customize the rewards and incentives, and it’s been fun redeeming as well. My kids are six, nine, 11 so the interest in how the app works is different for all of them. But it works really well, when you can make your own incentives. Having some thing to encourage consistency in our lives has been super helpful!
author: Ptreml

title: Even works on teens.
body: I have boy/girl twins age 14 and a 9 year old. When I caught my oldest son cleaning his bathroom and his bedroom unprompted, I knew it was magic. The key with him is creating rewards he REALLY wants like v-bucks or even pizza for dinner. No weekly pizza night unless he’s earned enough to redeem it.  My teen daughter is all over it. She’s loves lists to stay organized and this is right up her alley. I have to still nudge the 9 year old but it’s easy just to say “how’s your Doter doing”?  They like being able to see each others’ Doters too. All in all, whether it continues to work or not, it’s the most effective chore app I’ve tried. OMG…the youngest just said “I need to floss”. 😱
author: Box26

title: Motivating
body:
This app is so motivating for my kids. Not only are they motivated to get their chores done so they can take care of their pets, they can also earn real life rewards that I set. They are constantly asking me to add new chores so they can earn more coins. They have never been so excited to earn coins. The paid version is excellent, but if you can’t afford it, the free version works too! You just need to consolidate tasks so that you can fit it all into 7 free tasks. But I recommend the paid version if you can afford it. It really helps to have each little individual task on there to keep the motivation high. 

Customer service is great as well. We had an error message we couldn’t get past, and within MINUTES of emailing customer support, one of the owners had not only reached out to me, but had the issue completely fixed.  

As a former teacher, and current learning coach and parent, I highly recommend this app. It has made a huge difference for our family.
author: Mama2.5

title: Neurodivergent Family Friendly
body: Joon has been a welcome addition to our family! My husband, my daughter (4y) and myself are all diagnosed ADHD and this has been a lifesaver in helping us manage all the stress of chores, emotional regulation, health, and daily tasks. As you can imagine, the mental load in a fully ADHD household is a monumental struggle and Joon helps us ease the load. Our daughter is more willing to complete tasks and enjoys the feeling of success when she completes a tasks. She really enjoys keeping up with her doter and loves that she can interact with the app herself. The support I’ve received by the developers and staff at Joon has been great and I’m thankful for them!
author: Cayrene

title: Seems to work well
body: My teen is addicted to games. I just want him to take care of his responsibilities, honestly. I’ve tried the allowance and everything else I could think of but his willpower to be lazy was stronger. I found Joon and decided why not. Set up was easy and straightforward enough. So that was cool. I like all the options to set amounts, set rewards, require a photo or text, etc. If he cleans the bathroom but does an awful job, I can deduct points or let him retry or whatever. That’s also cool. He hasn’t redeemed anything yet so I can’t speak on that. Also I haven’t seen his side of the app. But I like the parent one ok.
author: Mlmndtr

title: Loving it!
body: My son loves the app. It definitely motivates him to earn coins to purchase different incentives. It also helps him to keep track of the tasks he needs to do for the day which helps him to be more independent. Definitely recommend it for children with adhd since there is the instant gratification with the game but also provides a visual for working towards longer term goals. Thanks Joon for helping our family out!
author: EmandWy

title: Huge motivator
body: My kids (6 & 7) both love completing quests and taking care of their Joon pets. It’s been a huge motivator for them to check off those simple daily tasks/chores children typically fight us on. Now they race to bring in trash cans, unload the dishes, etc to check off those quests. So many amazing features that were well thought out by this company.
author: Heartmomof2

title: Amazing
body: I have been struggling with having my 2 kids aged 7/9 (1 with ADHD) to stick to routines and we’re also dealing with anxiety and tantrums throughout the day. This app has been a lifesaver!!! Both of my kids can’t wait to start their routines morning/noon/night. What a great app to help kids learn the importance of routines/help parents reward positive behavior and it’s fun!!! In addition to normal routines, I’m also using it for things they’re struggling with (i.e. no thumb sucking, no tantrum at bedtime, etc.), for promoting positive behavior (i.e. random act of kindness, talk about emotions before getting mad, etc.), and to get them started on chores. Overall, I am super impressed with this app!!!
author: Scarola12

title: Fabulous tool!!
body: This app is working so well for getting the kids to do their chores!!!  They ask for more tasks and responsibilities so they can earn more points and play!  Fantastic way to ingrain good habits!
author: jacathow

title: Awesome for boys age 9 and 11
body: My kids have never been more excited to get things done- from personal care task, chores, school work, and other enrichment activities. It makes it so easy for me to not have to re invent the lists everyday and for me to not have to nag so much!
author: bhelvey

title: A more peaceful home
body:
My 8 y.o son loves his little buddies on Joon. He’s really matured, developed more independence and focus in just a few weeks using this app. When we go on outings, he often will ask me to bring up his app so we can take a picture of him with one of his buddies. 
I feel like I spend so much less time reminding him to do things. He’s motivated by the Quests.
I love that Joon provides such a wholesome environment for kids. Parents really have total control to personalize tasks and add in special rewards that are meaningful for your child in addition to what they can purchase for their buddies.
I just wish that I had tried the app sooner!
author: BetsyB08

title: A very useful tool
body: My 10 year-old Autistic and ADHD son is very resistant to even the most basic household and personal maintenance activities. So far Joon has been helpful in motivating him to complete these tasks more often. I suspect that as this app becomes a bigger part of our routine, it will become even more valuable to a productive and peaceful household.

I haven’t asked them to get dressed and brush teeth in a week since we started playing. They cannot play on the app until the tasks are complete, and I get to approve the tasks were completed first. They are not complaining about completing tasks and have even asked for more. My kids are 7.5 years old and 5 years old.

There are some glitches that need fixing- the kids can’t play the fruit catching (Fruit Party) game, their doter won’t move. Asteroid Adventure is frustrating- my son keeps complaining the asteroids are glitchy. My daughter just got her third doter but isn’t able to claim it - when she tries to name it, there’s an error message that keeps saying that the field is required to continue.

title: It works!

title: Great rewards based system for ADHD (8yo)
body: This app so far has worked well with motivating my son to improve/change his behavior using this reward based system. Very well made. Highly recommend.

author: juzonyi

title: Awesome app!

She now makes doing her chores and getting ready her top priority and with the help of the mental health quests, she has almost completely stopped having meltdowns. I would recommend anyone with a child that has ADHD or any child/parent that may be struggling give this app a try. IT ONLY TOOK 2 DAYS TO SEE A DIFFERENCE IN HER BEHAVIOR!! With a 7 day free trial and a quick turnaround in behavior, it’s worth trying!
author: mamawolfe32018

title: Amazing

I can’t believe how effective this app is for motivating my 5 & 6 y/o boys to take care of their responsibilities. Before Joon it was whining, crying and the standard power struggle.

Highly, highly recommend.

title: This App is Amazing!
body: This app has definitely stopped the fighting of who does what chore in this house. My younger 2 have had to pay for screen time and treats and free play. It has helped so much in the screen time and “I want this” department. They love competing with each other on who gets more coins and how many eggs they hatch. They also love pleating together with their different pets and buying them outfits. This is an amazing app overall. My oldest who is 15 even likes it. She has gotten chores done no questions asked. It’s nice not needing the constant reminder. I think the best part is that my youngest who can’t read yet, the app reads to her her chores and directions on them so she doesn’t have to consistently come to me for help. Absolutely marvelous app! I highly recommend to parents with higher functioning, screen addicted, autistic, ocd kids. This app is amazing!

author: Blue Eyed Samurai

title: No More Nagging!
body: No more “I’m bored”, no more forgetting, and no more groans about chores! Joon has changed how my family does chores, reminders, wellness, all of it. My kiddo is excited to see the coin stash grow, and I’m thrilled I don’t have to nag. Chores are actually getting done now! 🙌 I love that you can create your own quests, add a bonus reward, and mark things complete on the parent’s end without the child having to do it. When my son gets bored, I tell him to check his Joon app, where I’ve plugged in all sorts of different activities and ideas he can do. You might ask: should he get rewarded for building something out of Legos or Knex? The more appropriate question is: should he be rewarded for doing something he enjoys away from a screen that engages all those great STEM skills? Yes, absolutely. Both of us have ADHD, and this has been a total game changer. The biggest hurdle with chores and homework is the vacuous lack of dopamine provided by these activities. But earning virtual coins that can be used to purchase a reward? There’s the dopamine kick we were looking for! We had tried sticker charts, marble jars, and even cold, hard cash, but none of them worked for us. Joon has, and for that, I am thankful. Way to go, Brad, Isaac, and Kevin!! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

title: Please make an app like this for ADHD adults
body:
Let me start by saying that my daughter does not have any of the diagnoses this app is targeted for. She is (thus far) a neurotypical eight year old. *I* do have ADHD, so I won’t be surprised if she collects the same diagnosis eventually, but she hasn’t so far. 

But let me tell you, this app has changed our WHOLE household dynamic, especially in the mornings! We are NOT morning people. Getting ready for school in the morning is usually a giant fight. Lots of arguing, foot stomping, yelling, and door slamming. Now granted, we’ve been using this app less than a week, but our mornings have been… pleasant? Calm. Collected. It’s like the body snatchers in here, y’all. My daughter is RUNNING through the house to do the tasks I used to have to nag, beg, and scream for her to do. On top of that, she is actually ASKING me for extra chores she can do to earn more coins. I am blown away. 

Related: developers, please make an app like this for adults 😂 Maybe I’ll tackle my own to do list on a more consistent basis if I have a dragon to play with.

author: xxAS19xx

title: Great start, needs improvement
body:
This game has the potential for great things.  It’s a great start.  But I probably will not be renewing my subscription after the free trial.

I am not happy that there is only 1 currency in the game.  That one currency is used to buy everything in the game.  Be it berries, pets, in game activities, as well as the real life rewards I set up that I am aiming for my kids to earn.  This game is geared towards younger kids who do not understand the concept of “if I spend my money here, I won’t have it there.”  My teenagers think the game aspect is too childish.  So my younger kids are wasting all their coins on berries, in game pets, in game activities, and then upset because they never have the money to buy the rewards that I set up for them.  If I bump up the amount I give them, then they just spend more on in game shops.

There is a better option that could make this game even better.  They need to incorporate a second currency that the developers set as a permanent rate per quest.  This currency would be for the items the developers are trying to sell the kids.  And the second currency would be what the parent/counselors set up and would coincide with the quests that the parents/counselors set up.

Another option, although not as good, is to give parents the ability to turn off buying in game stuff.  This would handicap the game however, but I would rather have this ability than fight with my kids about where to spend the coins they are earning for doing real life activities.

My personal feeling right now is that all this game is teaching right now, is to work really hard in real life so you can spend your hard earned money on in game items and then be upset because you have no money for real life.  This is going to create bad habits for my kids in the future.  Sure there’s a few things I can do, I can do this or that to get around these issues, but by the time I put the time and effort in I might as well just go back to my old way that doesn’t include wasting hard earn time/money on a game.

title: An AMAZING tool for neurodivergent families!
body:
We started using a digital to-do list with our kids (now 10 & 7) a few years ago & it was a game changer for our family. Mornings, the after school transitions, & bed routines all became FAR less of a struggle. However, it was still a challenge to use and update regularly - especially when my husband and I had low-energy days. 

But Joon has changed that completely!

Now the kids are excited each day to check in with their pets (Doters) & the way the app is set up makes it SO easy for the parents to maintain! The kids (of course) don't love chores, but the way Joon takes that into account, too (you assign more coins to tasks that are harder to get them to do). We were able to transition their task lists over, and the system works better than ever!

We've been consistently impressed by all the features the app offers & how well it's designed for both neurodivergent kiddos AND their parents. It's fun to see how each kiddo uses it differently, too & how the app can accommodate all their needs with ease. One kiddo uses a kindle, and the other an iPad - and one focuses on growing their doters & camp, while the other is just trying to save enough coins to earn a family sleepover & movie night 🤣.

It's amazing, and I highly recommend it for anyone with kids!! The only thing I wish is that there was one for adults, lol.

author: anneal6510

title: My 7 & 8-1/2 ADHD boys are so motivated!
body:
I am a new user and was not paid in any way to write this review!! It is true and my experience with the Joon app. 

I saw an ad on Facebook and thought this couldn’t hurt in trying to get my child to do simple things. I loved that we could try the app with a free trial week. My struggles were with motivating my kids to even do everyday hygiene tasks without me constantly hovering over them to make sure it gets done and done correctly. You can only imagine how difficult it was to do anything!

I discussed the app with my husband and we reviewed what the recommendations were from the psychologist to help my boys have better daily functioning living with ADHD. Daily to-do tasks were one of the items suggested. We agreed if this worked, then we would continue with the app past the free trial. 

Well, we are a SUCCESS story! 

I got it all set up on both my boy’s iPads as well as mine. There are examples and suggested quests (activities/chores) for your child to complete. You can utilize the templates and also create and customize your own quests. There are many flexible ways to assign the tasks on when it needs to be completed. You can make them mandatory or optional, what time of day they need to complete by (Morning, Afternoon, Evening), and if they are Time and Day specific. There is also functionality for the child to take a picture of the completed task as proof they finished the quest. If they did a job halfway, you can send the quest back and have them “retry” with feedback on what needs to occur. You then set a reward value in the form of coins that they will receive for each successful quest they complete. 

Then, here is the part that I think most parents who struggle with and think that this app does nothing is that those parents are missing the mark on what or how to motivate their child(ren). The motivation is in the REWARDS that the children can exchange accumulated coins into REAL prizes that mean something to them. My suggestion is to sit down with your child and ask them what things or activities they like, what things my be perceived as restrictive or constantly withheld due to poor behavior choices, so that they can earn the privilege to have it, even if only temporary. The type of rewards should be attainable and a vast scale of lower value to higher value rewards. This allows them to feel a sense of gratification that they can earn a reward for successful behaviors we are trying to improve by either redeeming for smaller prizes or delay gratification and save for a larger prize. You also have the ability to award coins for things/positive actions completed that are not listed as a quest. BUT the KEY is you as a parent need to figure out and customize what motivates your child individually. This is where you will see success, in my opinion. 

My boys get up early or at the alarm clock time and are eager to start their morning quests, then after school, the completion of their afternoon quests are done and so forth. They even ask for more quests. They also tell me new rewards they would like to try to earn. 

We are currently on a great path to have behaviors that were once impossible to complete, to now having good habits and behaviors being formed and individual tasks completed without me even having to ask or, in their eyes, nag. 

On a side note, the customer service at Joon was amazing and superior! I had made a big mistake and deleted established quests instead of skipping them on several days when we were out of town. I panicked because I didn’t desire to re-do entering the quests. I messaged customer service and explained my problem and they promptly responded with solutions and reinstated the lost quests. I was so very thankful. 

In all, give the app a chance, think out of the box and involve your child as much as possible and you should see great and positive results.
author: Jeff's Beloved

author: flickering bucket

title: Effective app - has helped my very reluctant and defiant tween want to do chores
