Started using the app a couple weeks ago and my 11 year old who I struggled with to get simple chores done is now happily completing them daily to earn custom rewards I’ve created on the quests.
Def recommend creating custom quests and rewards, takes a little time to customize (maybe an hour of focus to set it all up) to determine how many coins each quest should be and how many coins each reward should be, but then they’re motivated to earn them. Would recommend this product to anyone needing help with motivating their kid(s) to get things done.
author: Rose Gold Glimmer

title: Game changer for kids OR moms with ADHD
body: As a mom with ADHD, I honestly don’t know how I could consistently communicate and respond to all the habits and chores my kids need to do every day without Joon. Without Joon I was incessantly nagging (with little to no results), letting almost everything go (like no one would brush their teeth in the morning, or ride the bus, or make their bed or help feed the dog…because it would just feel like too much), or I would have to devote all my time to creating my own elaborate system, which would overwhelm me and so I wouldn’t even implement it (some moms can geek out on that kind of thing. I am not one of them). For critics of Joon who say it is just using video games to get kids to do stuff, I say, you don’t get it and you don’t know what you are criticizing. The difference in my kids, my home, and my mental state without Joon vs with Joon is night and day.
author: jeaniln

title: Amazing Family Helper!
body: I saw ads for Joon for months before finally trying it and man do I wish I had gotten it sooner. No one likes to be asked to do something a million times, so instead of constant reminders, I touch base a few times a day asking them to check the app and take care of their tasks. It has really given them autonomy and motivation to help more. We added a task of making dinner once a week and after our 9 year old made dinner last night which including multitasking to clean up as she went, she said “wow, now i see how much goes into keeping up with the kitchen!” 🤯 It is really opening their eyes to how much goes into maintaining a household!

The idea behind this app is genius, and works great with one or two kids, but could get rather cumbersome with more. However, it doesn’t. author: A mom that loves momming

title: Joon to the Moon!
body:
This app has changed our child’s life, as well as ours! He looks forward to accomplishing his daily quests and is excited by the prospect of doing a good job and earning rewards. It has helped him develop repetitive habits (clearing your place setting, getting ready routine in AM/PM, etc., that we have otherwise had a lot of trouble getting to stick without constant reminding/guiding and lost patience.

Thanks, Joon! It’s been only a few weeks, but the results are in. It works! Our child is happy and feels accomplished everyday, and future habits to lead to success are being instilled.
author: JoeZak77

title: Great
body: I have paid for the app and I am astounded at the success I have had so far. I have known since my son was 2-3 years old that he has adhd but he wasn’t diagnosed until age 7. My son is now 8.5 and has been on medication for a year. The medication helps but not to the extent of which my son needs. He’s still struggling with emotion regulation and anger. Since using the Joon app I realized a big difference when asking my son to do things. It helps pair hard tasks with something that promotes dopamine in the brain so he actually gets excited about chores. The other night he spent 30 minutes doing dishes and I awarded him 40 coins because for an 8 year old he did pretty awesome. Now when asking my son to do chores I simply remind him he will earn coins and it can go towards an awesome reward and he gets super excited and is more likely to complete his chores. I didn’t want to pay the $50 at first but after seeing the improvement and reading some of the parent resources I wanted to be able to experience everything the app had to offer. Now I find myself recommending it to others with kids who struggle.
author: Zebralocked

title: So helpful!
body:
This app has helped our family in so many ways. I love the feature of making my own quests and assigning them to the people that they are relevant to. I have 6 kids and even have my husband listed as a kid so he can take credit for what he does, too! One kid (5) has a 20 point reward “Wasn’t contrary at all today.” 

I also like that the points can be cashed in for real-world things. For example, we have it programmed to let the kids cash in 300 points for $5 or 270 points for $5 in their savings account to encourage a savings mindset. 

We have the side benefit of extra reading practice and like that the kids can have the tasks read to them. 

It is time to buckle down and get back into the routine of using the app regularly again. We’ve missed it and it shows. We went on vacation and didn’t use the app for a few weeks when we got back and it really showed in our children’s behavior as well as the state of our house. 

The app is still new and I can’t wait to see where the team goes with it. We are here for the support in managing our chaos.

And the 7 year old is into it too! She’s using it for homework and chores. It’s a great way for parents to offer an incentive that’s not more money or toys. author: Hooked081812

title: Setting routines and making it fun
body:
I am primary parent, I keep my child (7yo) on routine and structure because she thrives in that. However, when I went down for surgery with a 9 mo recovery window things got really rocky and my ADHD spouse struggled to keep the routines or make ones that worked for him and our child. It was effecting their relationship and my recovery as my child would come in asking for me to fix the routine and I was unable to. The answer was Joon, I figured there was no harm in trying it and the structure and rewards were built in. It turned out to a game changer, first it helped my spouse recognize he was not enjoying parenting and he struggles, which is why most things in that lane are left to me. Next, it provided ways for him to build a routine that wasn’t mine and feel invested in the day to day but more importantly he saw how much his positive feedback to our child made her smile.

We are only a few months into Joon and it’s working well. Thank you, Joon!

body: We have only been using Joon for a few weeks, but I have noticed a major difference in my boys. No more telling them multiple times to do something. They get excited to complete things to get more coins to take care of their pets. It has been a life saver so far. I absolutely love this app. And it was definitely worth the subscription.
author: tiffiemadd

title: Great Motivator!
body:
My daughter is 7 and recently got diagnosed with ADHD.  She is also very oppositional.  

We have struggled with keeping her on task.  I feel we've tried so many things.  They help for a bit then wear off.

Joon has been wonderful!  She loves the characters and was over the moon when she got a unicorn!  I love that we have control over the quests and rewards.  I can edit them if I see the need to and my daughter is open to discussing what rewards she would like.  If I see a quest is too hard, I can change it.  The sample quests were very helpful in getting me started!  

Having a long trial period is nice.  I do wonder if a lot of families struggle with paying the year all at once.  Maybe a 6 or 3 month paying option might be helpful.  

I reached out to Joon with a question and the creators responded quickly, heard what I was saying, and took my question seriously.  I really appreciate that.  

All in all, we love Joon!

body:
My 11 year old is really loving this app. It’s a great way for them to develop independence on tasks and to dos and visually see the results of that instantly, plus have a really cool digital pet. 

However, I wish you could make tasks school day specific or weekend specific. Or only have tasks populate with calendar events with your Google or iCalendar. We use a family calendar and it would be helpful to be able to have those populate for the child like “dentist appointment at 2:00 today” and then maybe prompt the parent to put in additional tasks for that day (“floss EXTRA WELL” or something)

Would also be great to be able to share with multiple therapy providers.

title: Game changer
body: My son has ADD and getting him to see through his menial daily tasks is havocs stress in our household. I came across this app and it really has been amazing to see do small or big tasks—on his own accord because he’s aware it leads to an award. I would recommend this app to any parent who struggles to have their neurodivergent child autonomously complete daily life skills and become habitual and keeping a daily routine. It works if you work it. Create tasks that are specialized and individualized to your child and follow up with rewards they actually care about. This has become part of daily routine and I see it staying that way!
author: it'sthecuttingoffpeopleforme

title: Works!
body: My daughter loves it! It makes it easier for her  to do everyday task! She loves getting coins for her little pets!
author: nic4tre

title: It’s great!
body: This app has made chores fly by. The cat is fed, the teeth are brushed, the cello is practiced, and the books are read. Now I’m the one behind on my chore of approving their quests!
author: EMABH

title: Love seeing our boy thrive
body:
Joon has been a game changer for our son. He is starting to become a much more confident and focused child. He beams with pride when he completes his tasks and gets to complete his quests in games. Highly reccomend!
      sdf
author: Jax8217

title: AMAZING!!
body: My girls are finally doing tasks and so proud of theirselves while doing them! It’s made chores and homework so much more fun and exciting for them!
author: Cvilleolivia2013

title: Life Saver!!
body: Chores (quests) have been a massive battle and Joon made a world of a difference over night. It givese my kids more control, and an interactive to do list, and instant rewards. They came up with rewards they wanted and were eager to complete quests to earn them. I do wish there were a savings account option so they could put some points away toward a large reward while still purchasing small rewards along the way. This is a new app and they are actively working on it so maybe they will add one soon! As a side note, my kids also were gifted a tablet with the app so if they don’t use the app then they don’t keep the tablet. That has been an added motivator, but not entirely necessary. They love the app and the in app games that become available when they finish their quests.
author: GregWilson

title: Motivated my children to actually do what they should
body: I have several kids using the app. What I like is the ability to make things mandatory or optional. Also, it’s like triple positive reinforcement. You can tailor it to your specific needs or use templates. My 13 year old on the spectrum is now actually taking care of her responsibilities (feeding her animals without help, brushing her hair and teeth without reminders, asking how she can help out, even started a gratitude journal.) It takes very little instruction to set up and get started and it has paid off so far, which is great considering where we started from…a place of frustration and exhaustion. This app has really helped motivate the kids which has helped me to lower my stress level and get back to enjoying them rather than constant redirection.
author: MamaLu81

title: App never works
body: The kids app never works
author: Mithai77

title: Life changing
body: This app has been really helpful for my 7&8 year old boys who both have ADHD. They know exactly what is expected of them and are motivated to complete their tasks because they love taking care of their pets.
author: BLB5688

title: Kids are loving it!
body: Didn’t know whether this would really work for my kids but they are loving it. The reward system is amazing (you get to create your own awards specific to your family, like “picking the show everyone watches at dinner or “sleep on mom and dads floor”) and they’re now brushing their teeth without me asking! That alone is worth the investment. It’s easy to use and setup and I love the option to make your own rewards! As soon as my kids saw Roblox Robux were a reward, they immediately got their tasks done. My daughter also is a pitcher in softball and to say it’s hard to get her to practice outside of practice is an understatement. But when she saw it was worth a whopping 20 Joon points, she now asks to pitch. I also love (and they do as well) the option to make them show you a photo of the task completed especially for cleaning their room, or making their bed. Overall, I think this app is great! I had one issue in the beginning but Brad was quick to email me with a solution, unlike many of these apps where you can get no one to help. These guys seem like they truly care. Give it a try, our family loves it!
author: MKG9

title: Very helpful!
body: Our 7.5yo daughter was struggling significantly with morning and nighttime routines. Joon has helped her be more independent. I won’t pretend everything is perfect now, but she’s definitely much more on track than before. Much less arguments, too. She loves her pets and is motivated to get her steps done to take care of them. The app is easy to use for both parent and child as well.
author: MorganRam

title: Love!
body: I downloaded this app about 2 weeks ago to help my daughter better manage her time in the mornings before school. She needs pretty constant redirection when getting ready for school. Joon has helped so much! She is so excited to earn “coins” so she can feed and care for her pets. I will say there is a learning curve for the parent side, but I was able to figure it out pretty quickly.
author: GigiStar80

title: Great keeping kids on task
body: The kids enjoy doing the quests and the feedback they receive in the app
author: Great app!!! :)

title: Fabulous App
body: This app has fantastic for getting my kids to get things done! I had found myself yelling constantly for them to do the smallest thing around the house! Now I am not yelling! I remind them to check their quests and they get things done!!!! If you need help getting your kids motivated the. This is the app for you!!!!
author: Amalthea1181

title: So close to being great
body: This app has certain features that we love and we’ll continue using it for those features (the flexibility and clarity with the tasks or “quests” allows us to set very clear goals, adjust all settings like amount of coins it’s worth, set reminders, timers, etc. And the ability to set our own rewards that she is actually interested in earning). First of all, the graphics are HORRIBLE- reminds me of a gigapet from the 90’s. The 3 options of pets are ugly and weird, all the accessories for them are also eh, my daughter has no interest in playing the game part of this app. If it was cute fluffy animals, even lost a cat or dog, she would use it. Also it’s so complicated and difficult for us to figure out how many coins she currently has- I can’t see anywhere from my parent account and even in her account it takes some clicking and searching. But that’s the most important thing to her- to know how close she is to having enough coins to get the reward she’s working toward.
author: KMp386

title: This app has been a lifesaver for our family
body: My 8 year old ADHD child is very much incentive driven and this app is the perfect solution to get him motivated to do the things he doesn’t want to. It took some effort on my part to customize quests, rewards, and a point (coin) system that works for us, but it was well worth it! He is hyper-fixated on video games and so we made 1 hour of screen time one of the rewards. It helps keep me accountable when I say he must earn it! I also want to shout out the amazing customer service. The app stopped working on a holiday and the co-founder responded right away and had it fixed within the hour! I can’t wait wait to see how this app continues to grow! Thank you!
author: Kryswak2

title: Joon app
body: This is an excellent app! After I got it setup and my son onboard he’s waking up on his own and getting dressed. Taking his vitamins, doing his PT exercises and reading before screen time. Definitely try it out!
author: Eryca M

title: Needs improvement
body:
I love the idea of this app, and it definitely motivates my kids to do their chores, but the app itself has some significant limitations that keep me from giving it higher stars. My biggest complaint is the photo verification. The photo is tiny! There is no way to make it bigger to be able to actually see if my kids did the chore. One of the main reasons I chose this app was because of the photo verification, and it is pretty much useless. The app is expensive enough that I expect to be able to actually use the photo verification, and I don’t think it would be that difficult for the developers to add the ability to tap on the photo to see it larger. If this ONE THING was fixed, the app would get two more stars from me. 

Aside from the photo issue, the scheduling could have a few more options. I would like the ability to add weekly repeating chores, or quests, that would be available for anyone to do. For example, if they want more points, they could weed the garden or detail the car. But as it is, if I add the task repeating weekly, it will add to each child individually, but I don’t want it done three times weekly (once for each child), only whichever child decides they want the points and does it first. I hope that makes sense. I would also like the ability to add repeating weekly tasks that can be completed at any point during the week instead of assigning it to a specific day. 

If all of these issues were fixed, I would give the app five stars. The motivation factor is the best part of the app for sure.
author: Kimiftn

title: Doesn’t help
body: My son has been using Joon for a month and it has done absolutely nothing to help change his behavior and/or motivate him to do things when asked. I’m very upset that I have already paid for it for a year - waste of money.
author: JS1018

title: 4yr old undiagnosed ADHD
body:
I love the concepts but since my 4 year is not able to read and just like to click around, it wasn’t very helpful to get him to do his routine. You can add pictures but still wasn’t visual enough for him. I tried to show him the option to click to listen but he was still not interested in that either. 

He’s in the phases that he think he doesn’t need assistance to move through the app but often gets frustrated cause he doesn’t know but doesn’t want my help until its too late.

I do want to try again with this app after he learns to read but just doesn’t work for us right now.
author: Lady_tee19

title: Makes tasks fun
body: My daughter has only been using this for about a month, but has started looking for things to help with, to get enough coins to get her reward.  It makes it fun for both of us and sometimes she even earns “bonuses”, which I feel helps build her self-esteem.  I did pay for the year, which I’m hoping will pay for itself in the amount of time I save reminding my child to do what she needs.  I’ve tried other methods, chore charts, etc but they weren’t as engaging and fun.
author: MNmommy17

title: Chores are now a fun game
body: Our kids would hate doing there chores, now with this app it’s become a game and they completely forget they’re doing chores.  We have 4, 9, 10 and 11yr olds and they all love it!
author: JQ1369

title: Extremely useful but the notifications could use work
body:
My son has the hardest time staying on track, so we’ve been using Joon to motivate him to complete daily tasks and his Sunday chores. Overall we’re pretty happy with it, but I wish there was a better notification system. My son forgets to log his completed quests and that’s the new headache. I’m also supposed to be notified whenever he completes a quest and I don’t get those notifications.

It’s a great app though and I would recommend it to parents that have kids with ADHD, or suspect their child has ADHD.
author: itsamerita

title: So helpful!
body: This app has been amazing for my family! It has helped us stay on track both with housework and homeschooling. I even made a child account for myself for my own to-do list and as an example for the kids. It is so perfect for my adhd brain! I can add things to my and the kids to do lists and customize rewards they can turn in their Joon coins for.
author: FireandPixieDust

title: My kids love this app!
body: This app has been so helpful motivating my kids to do their daily tasks and I love that you can add your own custom rewards. Thanks Joon!
author: RebeccaWaldron

title: LOVE- and suggestions
body:
I love this app. It is so easy to use and is feeling like it is going to be a real game-changer for my family. My kids honestly having ever been worried about playing the game but are seeing the coin accumulation of completing their tasks as the game!

Instead of being on everyone’s backs (not to mention remembering myself), I can pop my kids' responsibilities in the app and let it live there until it’s done. 

A few improvements that would make this perfect app ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️:
- the ability to enlarge the photos the kids submitted of completed tasks
-The ability to add a due date and have the task still show up everyday until it's completed. Our 13 year old has a hard time remembering homework assignments and so I add them each in as a task, but if I add the due date it hides it until that day.
author: Adena2209

title: Joon has helped us achieve more harmony
body: Prior to using Joon, getting the kids ready in the morning and to accomplish family goals/tasks felt like it required a Herculean effort on my part, particularly getting them to do the less favorable tasks like taking vitamins or self-care (showering, brushing and flossing, picking up after themselves).  Joon has greatly reduced the power struggle and the kids (6.5 and 8 years old, older child diagnosed ADHD) take great pride in completing as many quests as they can each day.  We are able to accomplish more daily, with less power struggles, and it has reduced the overall stress in our home.  I highly recommend it to anyone whose children are working to develop executive functioning skills!

title: Love this app!
body: My kids took to it very well.
author: ShelWeldon

title: Thank you!!
body:
Awesome app!! My kids love it and it is easy for me to keep up with. It has made my household run smoother and my kids more independent! I would highly recommend it.

title: Loving this app
body: My kids and I have been using this app for several weeks now. It’s been worth every penny I paid for it. I love that I can set chores for the kids and I don’t need to constantly ask “did you do this” or “did you do that” I can simply look at my parent app and know if they did or didn’t. I didn’t expect my kids to “play” on the game otherwise, but they actually do enjoy it. We limit screen time in this house, but they enjoy this game a lot. My kids are 12 and 8 so maybe it helps that they are a little older. It was a bit to set up initially, but like I said worth the investment.

title: My 7 yr old loves it!
body:
It has been hard getting my 7 yr old to focus when it comes to a morning and evening routine. Now that he’s in second grade homework can be hard to. He is motivated to watch them grow into adulthood and he also loves that he can redeem his coins for rewards from me as well. Definitely recommend this as part of your parent tool bag. Especially if
You’re child struggles with ADD

I am seeing more active involvement from my kids, more interest in learning real life skills, less arguing, hardly any pushback when tasks need to be completed. I am looking forward to seeing how much it helps during the school year!

We’ve tried other apps to track chores and give rewards and I haven’t seen anything stick for my 8-year-old.

body: Love the app, so do my kids. It’s been a really great tool in helping with time management, chores, and behavior!

title: My kids are doing so many new things!
body: I love this app. It has changed our world at home. My kids are excited to do the things I have set for them. I love that it’s also not just chores it’s also life things. body: My 2 girls, 8 and 10, have been using Joon for a couple of months now. So far we’ve had zero fizzling out. Make sure to make your own amazing rewards to keep your kids going! We have movies, zoo trips, slushees, etc available as a reward and it’s been tremendously helpful.   I’m genuinely saving hours a day in nagging. I actually like my kids a bit more, too. Highly recommend.
author: whitestonehomestead

title: The kids love Joon!
body: This works to motivate my kids and keep them on task for routines, especially in the mornings and before bed. So far the game has expanded sufficiently as they’ve progressed that they’ve not gotten bored.
author: Joon a win

title: Lifesaver!
body: I will shout to the rooftops how great this app is! I was so tired of nagging my kids (8 & 10) to do anything! They truly just didn’t want to hear it from me. But make it a game and they are really into it! I don’t have to ask them verbally to do hardly anything and they are getting themselves ready, accomplishing their quests, and feeling proud of themselves for doing it on their own! I love that I can spend my time with them teaching them how to do something and having quality moments as opposed to spending all the energy bickering about chores. I know this sounds like a bot wrote it, but I promise I am a very real Mom who is just really grateful that this tool exists!
author: CassRettig

title: Good app, some issues
body:
I love the ease of setting and completing tasks. The pets are cute. One issue we have been running into is that the coins awarded keep disappearing. My kid will go to bed with one amount and wake up without some of them.  There isn’t a coin tracking system so we are not sure why the coins are disappearing. 

Another issue is he lack of game play. There should be some mini games or addition things to do with the pets.
author: isjfdgjvjk

title: Child loves Joon
body: Joon has helped my child be more excited about completing quests (chores). She enjoys taking care of her pets and it has helped her better stay on track. A fun, easy way to keep her motivated and rewarded.
author: AJSHMDH

title: Instant change
body:
We have 6 kids so mornings getting ready for school are always hectic even when we are crushing it as parents.  Joon has been a game changer for our younger 3 kids (ages 10,8,6). 

Our 10 year old has ADHD and struggles to complete tasks and has difficulty obeying simple commands. 

After 2 weeks of Joon he jumps out of bed and immediately makes it.  Goes right to brushing his teeth, then gets himself dressed eats breakfast and puts his dish in the dishwasher!  He takes his own medicine and then is ready to sit and take care of his Joon character!  This is a great app and tool to help incentivize our kids to stay within their routines and responsibilities.  We’re not the most easily impressed people and I’m not exaggerating when I say the results have been incredible!
author: Jake and Tan

title: Give the app a chance!
body: It takes a little while to get into the groove of things but give the app a chance. My kid is witty and he Instantly knew that this wasn’t a game and that it was an educational game lol. Just be open and talk to your kids about this game helping see that privileges need to be earned and this game helps with that. My son enjoys it and it makes him proud when he completes and earns things. In the beginning he was getting overwhelmed but I just did a few quests with him to show him that they are easier than they appear. Give it a try and stick to it for some time!
author: Mszouga

title: Life changing!
body: If I could rate this 10 stars I would! No more tantrums asking for screen time! Our 7 year old knows to check her app to complete quests to earn the time herself! Homework, chores, getting dressed in the morning, and more are all easier with this app! This has brought independence to our kiddo and peace to our lives!
author: Chrystine618

title: Life saver
body: Have 4 boys under the age of 8 and they all needed help understanding what was their age-appropriate chores. This helped customize their chore chart and make it very accessible.
author: Game changer app!

title: Life changer
body: Since there was a free trial before purchasing the yearly subscription, I decided to try this out. My oldest is 11 and while she likes her pet in the app, she isn’t motivated enough for it to make a huge difference. I’m still having to constantly remind her to complete her basic daily tasks (we call them tasks not chores). She said the app feels a little childish for her age. However, my 9 year old who has combined ADHD absolutely LOVES this app! It’s her new favorite “game” and we went from daily power struggles over everything from showering to cleaning her room, to her now asking for even more tasks! Within 24 hours her entire attitude changed, a week in and she is still extremely motivated. We all need extrinsic motivation, so why wouldn’t we expect kids to also? This app is the perfect way for her to visually track her progress and quantify her accomplishments all while playing a game. She is proof this app works! I will be recommending to any parent with neurodivergent kids. I would also recommend for neurotypical kids under 11 years old.
author: girlmomma94

title: Awesome App!
body: This app has made our days so much better. Our eight year old WANTS to get his chores and tasks done so he can play the game and claim his rewards. We’ve involved him in both coming up with tasks and rewards so it really does cater to him. My only suggestion for future improvements would be to find a way to check off the rewards once they’ve actually received them. Not all of our rewards are able to be completed immediately (ex: pick an activity to fo with mom or dad) and it would be nice if we could keep track of what we still owed. Otherwise, no complaints and we’re a very happy family!
author: Kris101610

title: My kids and wife are all using this
body:
I downloaded Joon so my kids can keep track of their daily tasks from brushing teeth to putting toys away and bringing their bikes and scooters inside. They love it. 
Even my wife is using it to complete tasks and I approve of them all!
It does require a little bit of discipline to teach them when it’s okay to use a device with the app because I don’t approve of my kids using their devices without limitations. But they are soooo much more motivated to complete their chores because they want to feed and care for their virtual pets by earning points. I’ve also set up some real world rewards like spending more time at the park or making wooden stamps with me.
author: penn1221

title: Transformative
body:
The game has hooked right into our 9 and 13 year olds imaginations.  The quests structure really helps where we are weak in consistency and focus.  We just had a guest over and we didn’t have to do a mad cleanup dash to not be embarrassed to have her over because our kids have been working the tasks so regularly.

It’s been over two weeks and life has gotten so much smoother.  Thanks so much!

title: Great app!!!

author: ZepherRae

body: This app has been very helpful for our son’s ability to focus on his tasks. He enjoys having a list of what to do and the points associated with tasks. The game parts complement the focus and learning elements. He says “Joon rules!”
author: Briankhowe

title: Worth a Try!
body: My 7YO was just diagnosed with ADHD and ODD. We’ve been struggling between repeating the same instructions nearly every day, and behaviors at school. This app has been helpful in our day to day dynamic… for example, one of his quests are to have a positive attitude and do his best. The only complaint is there are a fair amount of glitches, but I look forward to continuing utilizing this as the company moves forward and continues improving!
author: Amy Bud

title: Game changer as a parent
body: I can’t imagine life with out Joon. This has been such an improvement to our lives!
author: Jarrada

title: Has potential
body: I like the concept of this app but it is clunky to use and confusing at time. I hope they update because it’s a great idea. I will be canceling after the free trial and will download again once they get more kinks out.
author: Spaztsstic6

title: 10 year old
body: Love the app! My 10 year old is loving it and having such fun completing all her tasks throughout the day! Instead of being upset with tasks, she’s actually excited and doing things unprompted !
author: NomiMM

title: Helping the whole family
body: My 9yo has trouble with executive function and bed time has been awful for years. Fighting about the routine, him getting upset and lots of yelling. I tried Joon to help him with bedtime but it is making a positive impact on our whole day. Takes the pressure off me to get him to do things like take his vitamin or brush teeth in the morning. He loves the doters, too. There’s some trial and error setting stuff up but I love the control that it gives the parent. My ONLY issue is that the app does not work well when we aren’t on our WiFi. His device doesn’t have data and we’ve tried connecting it to a hotspot but it still doesn’t really work. I am giving 5 stars anyway because I’m not sure if it’s the app or his device that’s the issue. After 48 days of using Joon, I can officially say it was worth the price.
author: Cigrev

title: Great for my family!
body: I have a 6 year old with ADHD and this app has been amazing for my family so far. I am able to plan out my child’s day and provide her with opportunities to earn coins. She saves her coins to earn rewards that she has chosen which is a huge motivator! She also learns how to save so she has enough money to buy food which is a priority over accessories and rewards. She loves the animals and the fact that she gets a new egg every few days helps keep her interest! It is still a new game so there’s lots of things that are being worked on and improved, but this game has been amazing for my family and our routine! Even my 4 year old uses it without a problem and is earning rewards and taking care of her animals. Definitely give it a try if your child is needing something to help them stay motivated to stay focused on tasks and keep you and your child on a routine in your home.
author: Pj347

title: Joon on Amazon fire
body: So far my daughter has been pretty interested in completing the tasks in a timely manner, the only complaint I have is I wish it was categorized by Amazon kids as an educational app as I have to give her full access to her tablet for her to interact with the app on her own instead of making her complete Joon quests before being able to use other apps.
author: KayRod101

title: Stumbled here by accident
body:
I was actually simply looking for a chore app for my kiddos aged 17, 15, & 8. They’re good kids, always do their chores, and I have a reward system for them to redeem certain fun things. Except it was a chore for me to keep up with theirs. 🙄 

 I was poking around Joon and really enjoyed it, but after playing with it during my free trial, I decided to not get it. My kids are with me every other week and we have a big age gap. Just felt too complicated. So of course, I let my 8 year old take full advantage of the free trial. He fell in love. My bad. Dang it. 

 Before the trial period was over I received an email asking if I needed assistance setting it up. I replied my son was enjoying it, but I was going to cancel because of our unique situation. 

 The reply was incredibly personalized, attentive, and generous. Additionally, they did something on their side and we t above and beyond in service. I subscribed for a year, and my kids are loving it. 

I’ve pretty much automated the entire process - and both myself AND my kids kinda enjoy the fun kickback that come with doing our chores. We haven’t even explored other options, this app is so in-depth… I wanted to get in the habit of using it for what I initially wanted it before I added in behavioral aspects. I’m in love.
author: she.speaks

title: Kids not really interested
body: They liked it for a day but not much to do in the game really
author: Whitrshoes

title: Solid Solution for Motivating Kiddos
body:
Both my boys (4,7) are both doing their chores without being asked, they are asking for additional chores or tasks to help out. And in return they get a fun little digital creature and a garden and they are starting to unlock stuff.

Overall if you are on the fence at least try the trial. My kids jumped in so hard, and it was an easy decision to keep it.
author: StephAnn2

title: No more fighting
body: Love this app! My kids are excited to help and complete their quests. They are learning the importance of self discipline and working towards goals. We also don’t have daily fights about what needs to be done anymore.
author: Shanna M.Tok

title: It helps
body: Brad, Isaac, and Kevin are a great help with getting my kids to want to get chores done. They are able to care for a virtual pet that they want to keep alive while also earning coins for goodies like ice cream or money or Starbucks, etc. so far it keeps them interested. Thanks guys.
author: game tix

title: Just right for my 6 and 9 year old kiddos!
body: We’ve been using Joon for a few weeks and it’s been a big hit at my house. We’ve previously used paper checklists, which I felt like I am always micromanaging and constantly needing to update and print. This app is creative and engaging. I love how easily I get set things up and make changes as we use it more and more. I would highly recommend this for any family with young kids you want to motivate to stay on top of this responsibilities with some independence.
author: Bloom Women's Center

title: Life Changing!
body: Before Joon, daily routines were a fight in our household. We have been using Joon for about 2 weeks now, and the difference is astonishing. My daughter willingly goes through daily routines a majority of the time now- even the ones that aggravate her sensory issues. Joon is a lifesaver in our household!
author: AKHJMH

title: Great motivation
body: My kids are loving this app and so am I.  They are doing their chores and are excited to complete them!
author: Valerie 8

title: Works great
body: Gets the kids motivated to get their chores and homework done without complaining
author: ms.lolo56

title: Excellent App
body:
Got this app for my 10 year old granddaughter and she is doing well with it. She is completing tasks on her own and even looking at the days coming so that she knows ahead of time what is expected of her. She loves her pets though wishes there was more to spend her coins on. She’s only been doing this for a short time but would love to have habitats and be able to decorate them for her pets.
Anyhow, this is working out well and we’ll continue.
author: LoriLCrim

title: Perfect
body: This is all around the greatest thing I’ve done to help my child stay motivated and feel rewarded at the same time, all by getting things done without the hassle!
author: GennaB93

title: We are loving the inspiration it brings
body: My kiddos are 6 and 10 and the 10 year old is much more inclined to follow through with her chores. My 6 year old needs help and in the first week was literally asking “ can I floss my teeth now?!” So yeah, I’m hooked! I wish I could control push notifications a bit so I can remind them to do these things. The gamification of these quests is great! Keeps them engaged more than House a checklist for sure. Maybe some mini games as they hit milestones but as of now it’s been a few weeks and they’re both still checking in almost daily.
author: brookiebrooke22

title: The best app for families!
body: This is an amazing tool for families! My kids are engaged and actually following routines without me pestering them.  Their dad and I are divorced, but I can set up tasks in a way that keeps them following the same routines at each of our houses, while also individualizing some of the chores.  My son is high functioning Autistic, and my daughter is 6 and sassy, so we love that Joon also motivates them to curb some less desirable behaviors.  We love how it includes chores, routines, behavior, wellness - the full 360!  There are great suggestions for things to add, or you can customize and create your own. The same is true for setting up the rewards.  We can choose a nice blend of allowance money and fun activities - things that truly motivate our kiddos.  I can’t recommend this app enough!  It’s been a wonderful tool for our family!
author: BriannaElliott

title: Joon is great!
body: The app is really helpful in getting your kids to stick to a routine. It’s been great this summer!
author: zombie zombie zombie Ziggy

title: Love this!
body: We have been using this a month now. We had been nagging our child to remember his morning routine and to do chores. Now he remembers on his own and is motivated to help around the house and with his sibling! We have seen a huge difference in his attitude about chores and his memory! So many options for chores, behavior, social, etc. this has been a game changer in our home! It’s wonderful to no longer have to nag!
author: Boy-momma12

title: She wants to do chores!
body: Not every day - there is no such thing  as a magic bullet, but this has made so many days so much easier.
author: slcanna

title: Game changer
body: I no longer receive an attitude from my 7 year old son about getting dressed or getting a shower. He frequently comes down already dressed. He’s proud to feed his fish, take out the recycling, and pick up his room. Thank you, Joon!!!
author: ML_W

title: Changed our mornings!
body: We have fun getting stuff done now! We don’t have any morning before school fights anymore.  Truly magical
author: Stacie B.

title: Excellent chore management app
body: We are loving this app in our house!  Not only are there less arguments over getting tasks done, my child is more excited about doing her chores and is learning responsibility of taking care of her “pets” with what she has earned by completing the quests.
author: KMuj7

title: Great App!
body: This helps my daughter who is on the Spectrum and also struggles with ADHD to complete the tasks she needs to do each day without my constantly having to remind her. She actually proactively asks me to approve her “quests” so that she can play the game and take care of her doters. She has told me many times that she loves Joon and that it has helped her so much. It is well worth the investment to help keep my daughter on task with what she needs to be doing each day.
author: Modo82

title: Behavior-Changing App
body: I have tried several strategies to motivate my elementary child whom I suspects has ADHD/OCD. Getting him to do anything including flushing the toilet paper, throwing chewed gum on the floor, getting dressed without throwing a fit, etc has been a struggle. However, when a friend told me about Joon, I was willing to try (especially since I had tried everything else I could think of, AND I got a discount by using her code). Although my child still needs reminders, our first two weeks have shown drastic success. He loves earning coins to take care of his pet. An added benefit is that my 3 year old is also seeing big brother’s excitement, so she is helping out more to take care of her pet! THANK YOU JOON!
author: Jerajackson

title: Loving this app so far!
body: I ran across this app when searching for a way to help motivate my 11 year old (with ADHD) to do the things he needs to do throughout the day. I wasn’t sure if he’d think it was too “young” for him but decided it was worth a try and I’m SO glad I did! Both him and my 7 year old daughter are consistently checking for quests and completing them to earn coins. The amount of nagging/reminding I’m doing has decreased dramatically and that helps to improve everyone’s mood :)
author: LRLmom

title: Poor pricing plan
body: This wasn’t a bad app, but when I ordered it, there was no option for month to month pricing. And it’s not cheap. We used it for a couple months, but it became more of a distraction than a help. We only used it for about 2 months, but I had to pay for THE WHOLE YEAR, so I wasted a lot of money. I know, it was my risk, but most apps have monthly pricing, and that really turned me off to this company.
author: Ash492842837

title: Neurodivergent family
body: This really helps keep my kids on track with daily hygiene routine and chores and it’s super helpful. We really lean on this app to stay focussed. However it’s too expensive.
author: MissMcGray

title: My kid hated chores, but loves her quests!
body: My daughter loves taking care of her pet!  The constant arguing and repeating my self has dropped significantly, and we have only had the program a week!  It takes a minute to learn, but the ability to add real life rewards on top of game rewards is amazing!  We tried a reward chart, basic chart, clip board, limiting everything and nothing else has worked.  I am so glad we are finally heading in the right direction.
author: Michelle8900

title: So motivating!
body: My son absolutely love this! He is very motivated by getting his rewards and taking his care of his pets. He is completely his morning and night routine independently now! It’s taken so much off of me and his little brothers are following his lead, too!
author: Lblohm

body: For $90/year, would expect a troubleshooting feature. Deleted off both devices.  Next….

title: Very Effective

title: My 10 Year-Old Loves It!
body:
I was recently struggling to get my ten year-old to do his chores and decided to see if the game would motivate him as he really enjoys video games and I felt this would be an easy extension of that.

We have now been using Joon for over a month and he now comes to me to tell me when he os going to do his chores and to remind me to review his completed chores. He is much more cheerful when it’s time to clean and is now becoming much better at cleaning.

I’ve also found the design team is very responsive and open to updates and improvements to the app which I found very impressive and motivates me to use and share the app even more.
author: Hjones17

title: Transformational!
body: This App is so fun for our whole family. We have two boys, and we have struggled for years to stay consistent with any chore snd responsibility plan or system. And it has been a challenge to get our boys to do chores and responsibilities with out complaining. In one day we saw huge transformation and even fun attitudes towards completing responsibilities! I am so thankful I found this app and for all the ways it has brought more fun and eliminated negativity and frustration for our family! Highly recommend for anyone but especially parents of boys! Even our 13 year old son is responding positively to this app!

title: Greatest app ever for chores and family building!
body: Love it!
author: Boudy64

title: Needs more activities in the actual game
body: My daughter is 12 close to 13 and she loves animal  games when it comes to her adhd, but because there is only so much you can do with the pets in the game she got bored with the pets very quickly. You need more for the kids to do so that they want to interact with the pets and each other, more games. My daughter suggested more options of clothes to dress up with, more options of food to purchase for the animals. She said that currently the space ship game is too difficult and it glitches so she can only play the catch the food game and complained that its too easy and since those are the only two games on there, she got bored of them quickly. title: Great

It’s also easy to use and I do like that I can use this parent app to approve quests and everything straight from my phone. I would highly recommend trying the app.
author: KillerPanda…

title: Awesome Positive Reinforcement Tool!
body:
I am a mother of eight children, five have been officially diagnosed with ADHD. I had been looking for an app that could help me manage all that our household needed to get done. I was nagging my kids all of the time. Not anymore. Now I ask them if they have completed their quest or when they ask me for something ask them how many coins they have. Allowance doesn’t work in our house. 

The dopamine hit the kids get playing this game is exact what we needed. The first week we tried this, my eight year old son completed his two pages of homework by himself! That was a huge success! Normally our nights were filled fighting and crying. Not anymore. I am being truthful. I do not write reviews.

My fifteen year old daughter really struggles with time management. This app has helped her remember all of her daily responsibilities because that is how our family set it up.

My fourteen year old son is very competitive and loves to see that he has completed more quests than his siblings. He also likes to save up his coins for larger prizes. 

My twelve year old said he doesn’t mind brushing his teeth anymore and that he feels like he’s creating healthy habits.

My ten year old likes that he has a clear way to earn rewards and the terms are set. 

My eight year old just LOVES that it’s a game. It plays like a cross between Pokémon/Harvest Moon/Tomagachi. He’s all bout games.

My five years old likes to be playing a game like his siblings and that his tasks are attainable.

If you’re in doubt, just try it and remember that this app is a tool and not a fix all for our ADHD problems.

I love it! Love it! Love it! I tell everyone about it.

We use this as a tool. This will not solve all of our ADHD problems. Being a chee
author: Cinderella's Lady in Waiting

title: Expensive for What you get…
body: Cool concept, said it would give me a reminder before my subscription expired, which it did not, so $90 later, I have a subscription that isn’t really working my kids.
author: ctp5717

title: Not for us
body:
I have a 14 year old son and 10 year old daughter. I couldn’t get either one of them interested. I even tried to add a money incentive. They just don’t think raising a Joon is fun enough. My daughter (adhd) complains that she’s not motivated because it takes real life days, months to grow a Joon into full adulthood. It’s not compatible with her attention span. I think it would be better if it had a more complex game like prodigy, I don’t even have to ask her to play that, she’s on there constantly. 

On my end, it’s easy to use and I like the suggestions for tasks and all the different categories. It definitely has me thinking more broadly about what a well balance routine is like.
author: Marelinemerlan

author: Don’t miss this

title: Helps kids stay motivated to get chores done
body:
I have been looking for a tool that I can use with my 5 and 8 year old with ADHD to make the morning routine easier and keep everyone on task. Joon is the closest I have been able to come to perfection. I love that there are preloaded chores and I am pick the frequency of everything. My kids also like caring for their pets and buying them accessories. At the end of the week I look at how many coins they earned throughout the week and use this to determine how much allowance money they get. 

If you’re looking to keep a kid on task with a morning/bedtime routine this is a great way to do it.
author: RINYC

title: App’s creators really want your family to succeed
body: We have been using this for a short time with our seven year old son, who really struggles with completing tasks and independence/ownership of things. I was hoping to reduce the amount of nagging and task management I felt like our relationship had begun to require. We initially saw an extremely positive response from him re: the app. He was motivated and really enjoyed it. We’ve lost a bit of steam after the first few days, but I think part of that is because I got so used to him being self (or Joon)-motivated, I need to check in a bit more and make sure we remind him now and then about his “quests”. The app’s creator has personally checked in, responded to communication and asked for/taken feedback from us multiple times, and customer service has been excellent. You can tell they honestly care and want families to succeed. I am hoping our progress continues, and will provide an update!
author: atkofam

title: Motivating

So far it as kept us from arguing over tasks and getting out the door.

body:
This app has greatly helped me to get my son who is ADHD and ASD to do tasks.  If I ask normally he typically has no interest and won’t do it, or takes forever to do it.  With this app he has goals and wants to complete them to take care of his animals.

I also want to add that the team is super helpful.  I have reached out a few times with suggestions and they are always helpful and find ways to implement those suggestions and improve the app.
author: Adhd mom 13

title: Has really helped our young kids get motivated and me stay on track!
body:
We have been using Joon for about 3 weeks and have found it to make a noticeable improvement in our family rhythms. I am using Joon with a 7 year old girl and 5 year old boy with personal iPads. They have no diagnosed conditions like ADHD, but this app is still very helpful. They really enjoy the game. Taking care of the animals is something they are definitely into at this age. The game is simple enough to use that my 5 year old can enjoy it even if he’s not utilizing the more advanced features. I love that there is an option to have every dialogue and prompt in the game read to the player. I have one reader and one per-reader and they have both been able to complete their quests without getting adult help to read them. I also love the option to add in rewards that aren’t related to the game, like having an activity with mom and dad or going to ice cream. These rewards really motivate for the long run.
I have expressed to the design team that it is somewhat cumbersome to manage the different “quests” (tasks/chores) that I give to my kids, and they have been friendly and responsive in receiving feedback. But whatever imperfections the app might have, it did not deter me from paying the monthly fee to continue to use the app- the results have been that good.
I do have a diagnosed condition and the parent app actually helps me organize and communicate what needs to be done in a much better way than just waiting for chaos or emergency!  
I recommend this app to any parents looking to help establish routines in their home in a positive, fun way without wall charts and papers and printables that require space, preparation and possibly more creativity than we might want to come up with. :)
author: JenniferWood913

title: Game changer!
body: I have THREE, yes 3 children diagnosed with ADD. Their executive functioning requires a lot of structure and scaffolding. Joon has helped me get out of the role of “task master” and allowed my children to take charge of their daily tasks at home. Less frustration for everyone in my house!
author: Mandakatejohns

title: Friendly, user friendly, open to feedback
body:
My daughter has suspected ADHD with her father recently being confirmed and suspected with me as well. So her chances are pretty high. She’s so smart and loves games so when her focus become harder and executive functioning skills began to be impacted, I started looking for games to make. But as a mom, working, and with medical difficulties of my own, I don’t always have the energy to execute my ideas. Joon is a great and easy way to motivate my daughter to complete her morning and bedtime routine and she has even began to ask / suggest things to do in order to earn more coins. She understands mom and dad have control of the game so it’s really cool to see her not only be motivated by the “quest “ which are her day to day routine, but also start initiating other ideas as well!! It’s been really good for her.

Brad, the cofounder, has been active and engage in discussion with me over the weeks leading up to trying and since. Feels good to be heard too

title: Keeps getting better with time! Love it!

title: Love the app

author: Bibidish

title: So glad I finally gave it a shot!!
body:
I have a 12 year old and an 8 year old. They are always eager to SAY they will help with chores, but the actual DOING of the chores is like pulling teeth and they drag their feet- a task that should take five minutes takes an hour. 

I’ve read about Joon from a few places and finally decided to take advantage of the free 7 day trial. I created a few tasks for when they got home from school and when my oldest got off the bus had him download the pet game onto his phone. Within 30 minutes he was sitting on the couch, backpack put away, bed made, lunch box cleaned with tomorrow’s lunch made AND homework completed. I was floored. 
My 8 year old had exactly the same reaction. I didn’t even have to give him direction. 

As a test, I added a task for both of them titled ‘empty the dishwasher’ and in the description “whoever does it gets the points”. I didn’t tell them I added it, but five minutes later, my oldest charges into the kitchen, brother on his heels ARGUING OVER WHO GETS TO EMPTY IT!!! (I encouraged them to share the task, which they did without question and was able to assign extra points before approving the quest)

That was day one. It hasn’t slowed down. When they get home, they check their quests- they take pictures of the completed task, I approve it, they feed their doter and explore the world. I’m strict on screen time, but when they complete their quests, I let them play a bit. 
Gamifying their chores and making it interactive is truly the most brilliant way to give them responsibility and after that first day, I signed up for the yearly subscription. 

There are a ton of great features- you can pause the game if you’re out of town or skip tasks/mark them completed, you can choose to require the tasks to be completed before they can explore/feed/care for their doter, you can assign more or less points for jobs well done or rushed, and Brad is so responsive- I offered a suggestion that kids be able to create their own tasks for approval and he is looking into creating it with the next update. 

Genuinely loving this app and the motivation it provides that the kiddos have been lacking to this point.

title: Kids (6 & 9) are actually into it!
body:
I figured it couldn't hurt to try the free trial and cancel if my kids weren't interested, but to my pleasant surprise they are! They have learned what chores give them points and have been excited to mark them complete. I still have to remind my kids to do their chores because they're not on their devices enough to get the push notifications themselves, but it does seem to be less of an effort to motivate them. The chores (quests) are easy to set up and assign, and it's easy for me to review the quests completed and give the kids their rewards.

I plan to explore some of the other types of quests other parents use (you can do this from templates) because I feel there are more things that could count as quests. I appreciate being able to use common quests that other parents have assigned because it helps provide inspiration! The "absolutely no physical violence toward sibling today" quest has been helpful for me (a parent template) but also validating for my daughter. She is proud when she can check that off because she has demonstrated strong impulse control and emotional management (ADHD challenges).

I hope the game continues to hold their interest, as we have been happy with these first few weeks!!

title: Great app for all children
body:
As a pediatric health care provider for children of all developmental levels, a person with ADD, a mom of three kids(2 have ADHD one does not), I love this app!  It aligns nicely with all of the recommendations on finding positive ways to motivate your kids towards successful behaviors. It is cheaper than buying them prizes, and better for their health than rewarding them with candy. It provides the instant gratification that kids want. 
My children are excited to do things to earn coins. They are doing their chores and school work without me having to nag them. They get on Joon each evening and check off all the quests they accomplished for the day. It allows me to see all they accomplished and give them compliments for their successes. They are all in the game together and can talk about their pets.  There is a little healthy sibling competition to earn more pets and coins. 
The game itself is fun and always changing so they don’t get bored. It is pretty calm and doesn’t overstimulate them before bed. The characters are really cute. It is fun to collect different ones and accessorize them.  The quests can be customized based on what your child needs to work on, but mostly I have used the ones that were given as examples to choose from. This made it very easy to set up and get started. 
I would recommend this game for any parents who want to find a fun and creative way to reward their children for doing the hard things they need to do. All three of my children love this game!  I love that I am not having to remind, and ask them about their responsibilities nearly as often.  It is a great game and worth the investment.

author: Fish&Sprout

title: Do yourself a favor-try this app today
body:

It is an app that tracks all of his daily activities in one place within an interactive game. 
The app developer is responsive and open to feedback to improve the app. The price is affordable and well worth the improved relationship with my 9 year old. I also appreciated having a trial period to see if I liked the app. 
This has reduced the amount of time I spend arguing with my son about all the things that need to get done daily. 
The app is marketed to kids with ADHD or on the autism spectrum. My son is none of these-just a high-energy, busy 9 year old. This app successfully helps him keep track of all of his tasks. Do yourself and your family a favor and try this app now, don’t wait.

title: Game Changer For Busy Parents
body:
Finding Joon has made such a difference for our 6yr old son! As a parent of a child with ADHD, it is so challenging to find the right combination of structure, consistency, and simple methods to support development of routines and independence! 

We have tried everything to keep our child engaged and motivated to do everyday tasks, and have failed so many times, until we found Joon!  

We are about a month into using this system consistently, and it has literally changed the  everyday experience with how our son manages transitions and independent task completion.  What I love most is the ability to customize the experience to support our child’s development needs, and the gamification aspect turns everyday tasks into FUN as my son completes his before school, after school, and evening “quests”! 

This is truly an app built to support children with special needs, whatever that looks like for your child - this could be the solution for you, as it is proving to be for our family.. thank you to the Joon Team for building something that is making a difference for my son.. More confidence, less meltdowns, better home and school behavior - worth the investment. 

Thank you Joon Team!

I took things a step further, and transferred their in game coins into an allowance (100 coins = $1). They’ve averaged $7-$10 a week allowance.

My one and only complaint is the number of notifications I receive. I like receiving a message when the kids complete a quest, but the “we just reminded your child to…” messages are unnecessary. 

Overall, I think Joon is a wonderful app and will be a great motivation for children to complete chores, routines, even physical and mental health quests.

title: Instant results on my child’s routine
body:
I thought it was too good to be true, but because I am a parent that is desperate for my child to improve on having a consistent routine, I gave it shot. I am so glad that I did! author: The Angulo Family

title: Just a great concept
body:
The app sounded perfect but it didn’t have the foundation to follow through on the goal.  The price is kinda absurd for what is offered.

As I said the concept is great!  I was able to select and create a perfect chore or task list and assign the jobs easily.

When my daughter completed her most important task for the morning, “taking her medication” she submitted it for parental review in order to collect her coins it never appeared in my parent app for approval.

So the immediate gratification which a child needs with ADHD; which the program offers didn’t work.

Secondly the game play is appalling.  The only “fun” provided through game play is feeding, petting and washing their pet after buying food with coins.  

They can also run around in the game.  They can buy flowers to plant, but we never got a prompt to plant them.  The field is very minimal.  So the game play provide: feed your pet, wash your pet(soapy bubbles appear over pet for 2 seconds while you move your finger) and run around the screen with no interactions while the scenery doesn’t change. It’s a green field of grass with a handful of flowers seen on occasion.

We didn’t waste more than two hours on the trial.  There’s no way my kids would be motivated to complete tasks with the same out outcome every single time they get their coins for the game.

No we would not recommend.

title: wonderful concept
body:
our seven year old uses this app and seems to enjoy it. The characters are very cute and he seems to like that aspect and loves taking care of them. He says he likes it because “it encourages you to take care of people and pets.”

It’s nice to be able to assign different point levels to each of the tasks. I think our favorite thing about this app is that we can exchange notes about the different tasks

It’s a really nice way to communicate with my child even when I’m traveling, I can send encouraging notes and response to his tasks. 

It sometimes has difficulty connecting to wi-fi and crashes occasionally, especially on his Kindle Fire. The app seems to perform better on the iphone so I sometimes have him completed tasks on my phone. 

The app has some games which he plays occasionally but not often. 

This app could easily be a five star app with a few modifications. The concept overall is excellent. 

Improvements would be - 

Adding another incentive besides the Doter characters. after using the app for several weeks he has numerous Doters and he sometimes worries there are too many and it can make him a bit anxious/overwhelmed. They hatch and age very quickly so it’s easy to have many Doters to care for.

Making it easier to see which characters need care. Currently he has to cycle through the full set of characters and it takes a long time to do. Because there are so many, he often loses sight of the quest list completely. this can feel especially burdensome in the morning when we have limited time to get out of the house to get to school on time.

title: Adhd mom and kids, love this app!
body:
Hello
I found Joon on the app store. It has been such a blessing in our lives! My kids love to earn coins and get doters (eggs with a creature inside) or explore new worlds. 
It has been GREAT at getting them to want to do chores. Even if it starts as a complaint, once they log in they seem to forget and chores become part of the game. Now *I* get bugged to check on their progress! 
It also helps me remember what needs to be done. I love, love being able to customize what they need to do each day of the week. With homework, chores and extracurriculars, this really helped me organize my schedule for them and then they see what each day looks like. 
I am trying to also build independence from this as well. They hear “go check your Joon” now. Once a routine is in place i might start to use the alarms to keep them on their own. Esp my 9, going on 10, year old. She loves this because of the independence it gives her. While my younger and more adhd child loves it because it keeps him better focused. 
Overall so far I could not be happier. 
Thank you Joon!!!

author: Struggling Mom of 3

title: Great for Accountability
body:
This is a wonderful app for kids, teens, and adults that want a more fun and collaborative way to stay organized with things that need to get done. It helps keep things manageable and allows us to give our kids more independence with handling their responsibilities without us needing to remind them all day. They know to check their Joon and they have fun doing it.

It’s also been such a great way for us parents to communicate with one another about different things that need to get done around the house, with the kids, or in general.

PROS:
- Fun
- Organized
- Collaborative 
- Flexible to your needs (anyone who needs reminders- use this!)

CONS:
- I do think price point is a bit high, even considering how much I like it. I wouldn’t mind if it was a 1 time fee but for annual.. sheesh. That being said, it’s a small business and I’m all for supporting that. 
- It’s still new so I mean, it’s understandable but the app does crash or get stuck loading every so often. Kids also have gotten logged out randomly a couple times. 
^ No other cons and the above isn’t too serious. We close the app and reopen and it’s fine. And bugs are always being worked on. 

FAQ:
- Yes to really use the app you need a subscription. There’s a trial before committing. There was a promotion so I ended up getting 1 year for $69.99.
- I’m not getting anything for this review. I just really like the app and it’s sad to see so many negative reviews from people who don’t use it.. just complaining over the price point.

author: EllieKay07

title: Has a lot of potential!!
body:
I am a 19yo who is struggling through online college. Set up this app for myself and found it pretty effective for the first day, yesterday. I actually just hit my free quest verification limit so I’m writing this before deciding to go forward.

First of all, the screenshots on this page look a bit different from the actual app, since the game is separate. Also, the “create an account” button on the game — does that mean you can make an account independent from the parent app? Little confusing.

Second, while the game is fun-looking and motivating enough for me so far, I do find the game a little hard to navigate… and there are other shortcomings as well. Obviously I’m really low level, so I assume there’s stuff to unlock and therefore I’m not going to point out how empty the overworld is for me. However, I think that my pet moves too slowly lol, and if I could zoom out more, swipe with two fingers to see the rest of the area, or move faster, that would be an improvement. Also, in the garden area, I think that the build button should be on the screen outside of the circle menu. Less confusing that way, in my opinion. The games are fine but some minor improvements (like faster music when the difficulty increases, and sound effects) could be made. And I don’t know if this is an unlockable thing, but the lack of menu chat (at least) in the plaza makes it sort of… useless?

On a more general note, I think that adding some more world-building stuff and lore could make the experience more immersive.

As for the parent app itself, I set the due date for a couple quests to be tomorrow, and now they only appear on tomorrow’s quests. Shouldn’t they appear for every day until the due date?

I also don’t know if you offered a monthly subscription before, but I can’t find it. I would really appreciate a monthly subscription over a yearly subscription.

Anyway, it’s a great idea and I’m excited to see what updates come in the future.
author: ShiningStarLuna

title: Good start, but could use some tweaks
body: While i LOVE the premise, I think improvements can be made especially for the price tag. 1. ADHD kiddos are dopamine seekers and can only focus on things that interest them. Kiddos can hatch all three allowed eggs in the first week, so after that, there’s not much to look forward to, or earn points towards, so it immediately loses interest as soon as the third egg is hatched. It would be great if maybe they had to take care of an egg for a few days in anticipation of it hatching. Then after that, space out the time before they can hatch another. Maybe the second can hatch after a could weeks, then the third a few weeks after that? But have a “timer” countdown until the next so they can see how much time is left. 2. Give them more things to do for their doters aside from feeding/washing/petting. I see they can buy rock and flowers, but for what? Allow them options to buy clothes, or change the doters colors, and personalize their characters. 3. Allow the doters to perish if they aren’t taken care of. Not right away of course, but if they aren’t fed for a week… This will create “urgency” to complete their tasks. 4. Are there other lands besides the “plaza” that the avatars can visit? Can there be mazes or puzzles incorporated? Something for them to do aside from walk around the plaza. 5. When in the plaza, could there be some kind of interaction feature added? Maybe not a full- on messenger feature as that could be a safety issue for kids, but can they send each other pre-loaded words of encouragement? From my 7 year old: “I would like there to be a treasure hunt on an island where I can find diamonds and gold and fight pirates”. Use this suggestion however you see fit, LOL!

author: F.England

title: Spread the word!
body:
We have four young kids (ages 6,5,3,2) and this app is SO AWESOME. Previously, I've been keeping track of their "points" on the fridge. I would go mark them off every time they did a job, etc, and every time they filled up the sheet, I had to make a new one, and if somebody knocked it off the fridge, it might get torn or wet, because, kids 😆. 

This app is perfect because the kids can "see" their progress and in a very accessible way. Even my 3 year old can navigate the app easily, after we helped him for the first couple days. 

Furthermore, I immediately noticed that the app has peaceful music playing- not overstimulating- and that the pets move in a slow, peaceful manner. Most kids games are sensational- drawing their attention with startling sounds and flashing bright colors. When they are in this app, it feels like a mindfulness exercise.

The suggested quests have been really helpful as a parent, placing value on meaningful activities besides just household tasks. I have ADHD myself, and I don't know if my kids do yet, but it's chaotic around here and this all has helped streamline and bring joy to our daily routine.

Really, I could go on and on. It's a young company and a new app, the co-creator personally emailed me in response to my questions and they are in the process of adding even more features. I never do this, but I'm sharing this app with whoever I can because I want to be sure it succeeds and grows!! 😍😍😍😍😍

title: Super helpful…for a while
body:
I’ve loved this app. As a teenager with ADHD and severe executive dysfunction, while I’m not exactly still in the target demographic, I’ve still found it very helpful. Unfortunately, once you’ve been using joon for a while (about two months in my case) you simply run out of content. I’ve bought everything the in-game currency can buy, with so much left over I could probably buy the whole shop again if I wanted. A couple of absurdly overpriced items would actually help a lot, since they would provide something to keep working towards. I keep waiting for updates that provide new content for the higher levels, but it seems the team is more focused on onboarding new subscribers than keeping their current ones engaged. Not that I’m judging them for that, I understand that they have a ton of work on every front.
All that being said, joon actually helped me form some good habits, so its value to me will definitely outlast the time I spent using it. I would recommend it to parents for sure, just keep in mind that the app itself will have a limited lifespan, so to speak.

author: Hybrtyu

title: A real relief to parents!
body:
My 11 year old daughter has ADHD and even with chore charts and lists she struggles to complete daily responsibilities. I would constantly have to remind her to check the list and to make sure she’s done them all. I would even have to remind her of what was on the list even though it was posted next to her bedroom door. 

This app has been a godsend from day 1! She checks it first thing in the morning and last thing while getting ready for bed. She’s even been asking me to add things for her so she can remember! She is adding more quests for herself and is showing SIGNIFICANT improvement. 

My only concern is that although we’ve been going almost a week strong without missing any days, I’m worried that at some point the game will not be as motivating as it once was. Are there new items that they can unlock after some time? Will there be new features added periodically? As an adult with ADHD I know that games can get boring after a while, and with this being an annual payment I’m worried I’ll spend this money and it won’t work after a couple of months. 

All in all I’m very happy with the app, and if there are new features or items added periodically, then it is definitely worth the money to not have to hover over and fight with my daughter every day.

author: mrs.lawhon24

title: Answer to Prayer
body:
Parenting is not easy and every kid is different and none of them come with an instruction manual on how best to help them. We have been struggling with how best to help one of our kids. They are amazing, but we were fighting about everything. If we even mentioned chores, he instantly threw a fit and there was so much tension in our home. It has been several miserable months. One late night I was praying about what to do and I thought maybe there was an app that could help. Joon popped up as an option and so I decided to give it a try.
My son instantly enjoyed having a “pet” avatar and loved the challenges and began doing his chores because they were fun and I didn’t need to be the bad guy. I love being able to leave him messages and give him positive feedback. I love the parent support this app gives, as being a parent can feel lonely and often without positive feedback.
Our relationship isn’t perfect, and not all chores, homework, etc. are done every day, but things are headed in a much more positive direction. This app has helped so much and I rarely spend money on any app, but this one has been 100% worth the money. Thank you so much for creating it.
