title: Day 1 and loving it
body:
Update: I have one more request! Well, 3…since I already shared some in my 15 min Zoom call. But I will share them all here. 
1. My son (7year old) needs a more visual representation of his quest. Like a path he moves down or “thermometer” so he can see himself getting closer to a goal. 
2. He needs a better way to print the goals/ tasks so we can have a visual of it when he is not on screen time.
3. I need to have the ability to mark off multiple items complete for him. Since he does not have screen time every week, and I have to catch up on a day or more… it’s driving me crazy to go back and do each one individually.
(One more)4. I want to be able to choose what he is going to earn. The items they have are not enticing enough. He wants to earn things and he wants to pick it out.

***********************************************

So far it’s been great! A couple of glitches. 1. I want to be able to mark things complete for the previous day because his screen time ends on his iPad and don’t want him to get on it again. And… I also have ADHD so I need to do it when I remember. 2. I can’t seem to have things happen in the morning and at night. It shows up as 2 in one time slot. He needs to take meds in the morning and at night. 3. Make the music turn offfff!! I click the switch and it just stays on. He wants the volume up for the immersive reader. But the music is blahhhh! Keep up the good work on this!

title: Challenges + rewards = happy (ADHD) kids
body:
I tried many of the popular chore apps on the App Store in order to get a feel for each before presenting them to my kids ( 7 & 8 years old). Many were complicated, involved way too many steps, or were geared toward an older crowd with their own devices. We couldn’t find a fun, simple, and straightforward chore/reward app that my kids could operate without involving me. 

Joon presents itself as an engaging, goal-oriented, and responsibility based app for kids. First and foremost, my kids know they must take care of their Doter. They love checking in to make sure it is fed, bathed, and awake.  If they don’t, the Doter becomes neglected, then falls asleep hungry and dirty.  Even more fun, they can peek in on other players’ Doters to see how they’re faring. My kids felt pretty proud of themselves when they saw many other Doters were asleep or dirty while theirs were thriving. A sense of pride and responsibility instilled by an app? Check. Motivation to keep doing well in their chores? Check. Oh, and completing the assigned chores earns points and coins. They can use those coins to purchase items for their Doter in the special general store. 

Adults can use preset chores (referred to as Quests)  or make up their own. Joon is the most user friendly app I’ve tried so far and what has sold me on using it long term. 

Lastly, the creators are communicative and appreciate feedback. I like that they want insight as to how the app can be improved.  This app is definitely worth a try and I recommend it for any families that have game motivated kids or those who want to care for a pet.

title: The Perfect App!!
body: This app appeared in my IG feed after a particularly difficult day navigating my son’s struggles to stay on task. I immediately downloaded it and began customizing it to our lives. My son LOVES Joon and looks forward to spending time exploring and taking care of his doter. His little sister watches him play for hours and can’t wait to create her own! I’m particularly impressed with the customization abilities for tasks. It is easy to tell how much time has been taken to design both the parental side, as well as the child side. I’ve referred several friends and continue to bring it up whenever I hear someone struggling with their kids staying on task. Kudos to this team for their foresight into consumer needs, as well as their amazing communication. This app is honestly perfect for all kids, but it really checks off all the marks for keeping a neurotypical kid engaged. Thank you so much!

author: Mila Boston

title: Not great for kids w/ adhd
body: Unfortunately this app was recommended for kids w/ adhd from someone who supposedly had a 7 yr old w/ adhd, trouble completing daily tasks, etc., which sounded exactly like me son.  So we downloaded the app after the great rec, esp coming from a teacher, and come to find it requires a subscription after 1 week.  Due to my son’s adhd, he has a hard time regulating his emotions, and he has gotten upset every single time he uses the app.  If you have an empathetic? sensitive child, and/or ate not intetested in him playing yet one more video game disguised as something helpful, I would not open this can of worms.  when my son sees any of the doters, his or others, who look neglected (start to get dirty or havent been fed all day, start to enter some hibernation state- he says they look dead, he tried to help other doters but can’t, etc.  It has created an emotional roller coaster every night.  Along with the issues kids with adhd have playing video games (which this basically is), it’s been a nightmare.  Even having the conversation abput getting rid of the app- which he said we should do- he still gets upset thinking about “killing” off the doters he’s created.  I Feel very much like we were misled about this app from someone trying to take advantage of whatever monetary incentive you offer parents to get others to sign up.  Saying this app is developed or backed by experts in child development is nonsense.  No expert in the field of child development who has any ethics would push yet more video games as being a good idea for kids. My son asked me to write this review to warn others to stay away…

title: Great App, but…
body: It really is a very good app. I used it for the first free week. My daughter, who does not have self regulation issues, loved it and it really worked with her. Problem is, within less than a day, my ADHD son got OBSESSED with devices again, after we’d weaned him off. He could not focus on anything else except screen time. We got no schoolwork done because he’d be sulking or crying about it not being Screentime. As parents, stress levels went up because of additional outbursts and arguing about access to devices. Ultimately, with him, who was the “target audience” in us trying Joon, the negatives outweighed the positives.
author: camelotCPT

title: Great!
body: We love the Joon app! I would like to request bonus quests though. Quests that they can choose to do any time of the week if they want more coins. Also more variety in doters? The kids love it!

title: Transparency
body: The app requires membership fees which is not stated until you have downloaded it and answered a bunch of personal questions. Misleading.
